While the base focused on informatics security and computer science, it would enable Overwatch to respond to threats around the region, fighting Doomfist and his lieutenants from the outside, primarily through the efforts of a new Strike team member: Wildebeest.

The Horizon Lunar Colony had been a long-lasting success by this point, but Lucheng Interstellar was never aiming for the Moon. Their eyes always lie beyond the stars. So many years after the Moon base's establishment, the company felt ready to begin the process on the next frontier: Mars.

The initial proposal, however, was denied by the UN, but this did not stop Lucheng. They would keep the plans in motion funded internally, and begin gathering a group of scientists and engineers in the public eye. The small team was going to be the first phase of Project: Red Promise, a multi-stage terraforming Initiative to colonize the surface of Mars. At first, the project carried on smoothly, as the astronauts arrived on the red planet's surface and established a base within a matter of months. What none of them expected was that two of the team members, Dr. Jiayi Teo and Dr. Khiem Van Minh, were having a baby

As the years went on, Ana's marriage would eventually collapse, but it wouldn't be the end of her love life. Over the years she had grown quite fond of Lieutenant Reinhardt, who likewise adored her back.

However, with the messy relationships if her past and the dedication they both had to Overwatch as soldiers, life got in the way. Reinhardt, too, always put others before him, and understood Amari's need for distance well, those he never pushed on the matter. So went the years they shared in Overwatch, where they both quietly yearned for each other without ever saying a word of the matter, but the rest of the team? They all knew well what the looks they gave each other meant.

The more time passed since the crisis ended, the more governments across the world were back to full power, reinstating their policies and deemphasizing international cooperation. More and more countries were eager to prove that they could stand on their own in this new world, and began to hesitate about immediately allowing Overwatch for deployment. Morrison began to feel the weight of global bureaucracy, as lawsuits and protocol became too much to wade through and often allowed criminals to get away.

One particular mission came up that would allow Morrison to put Overwatch's charter to a test. The family of an American diplomat had been kidnapped and taken into Russia, and Morrison tasked Amari to retrieve her. Ana sidestepped protocol and did the mission before Russia approved of her clearance. Everything went well. She tracked down the terrorist and retrieved the civilians alive, but in the end, she was intercepted by the Russian government and charged with illegal entering and obstruction of local law enforcement. Ana was released, but permanently banned from Russia.

The so-called Xie Incident became a stain on Overwatch's reputation, as Russia had consistently been skeptical of allowing the organization inside ever since the Crisis, and after Ana's breach of protocol, those rare occasions only became even rarer. Ana's acts in Russia became a bit of a legend, however, with many exaggerated accounts of her feats and what led to her ban proliferating over the years.

On March 22nd of the year 2060, Juno Teo Minh, the first Martian, was born. Juno was a surprise to the Red Promise team, but in a lot of ways she embodied the hopes of the project, and everyone loved her as if she was their own kid. While the scientists were often busy with their duties at the base, they made an active effort to give Juno a happy and healthy childhood, but it was clear their curiosity rubbed off on the young girl. Having been born in an early colony with so few people, in a world so far away from Earth, Juno was quite sheltered and inexperienced with a lot of the ways the world worked, things that would be normal to an Earth-born human were completely alien and often terrifying for her.

It also meant that Juno was always eager to get out there, and see more of her home. She wanted to help the team join in expeditions on the planet's surface, and once she was old enough, they would provide her with her own space suit, allowing her to roam through the outdoors of the colony and aid the scientists on the staff, as a true member of the team. Still, she often fantasized about Earth, especially when watching the cowboy movies that her dad had brought with him.

The decade following the crisis saw the rise of the Omnic Rights movement, as it became clear to the world as a whole that the sentience was permanent and impossible to ignore, and Omnics themselves grappled with their place in the world. While cities like Toronto and Numbani made active efforts towards Omnic integration, the reality is that the world at large was generally far more hostile. From the cleansing of Ravager units, to the destruction of the Australian Omnium, or the inhospitable conditions of the London Underworld, to domestic units being thrown into the streets all over the planet, as their previous families rejected them or in worse cases, were forced back into servitude. Something needed to change, and here, so an organized movement began to campaign for the United Nations, seeking for global recognition of rights and obligations for all Omnics, to be treated with equal respect and empathy as humans.

When the UN finally took a stance on the issue, Liao was called as a witness for the case of Omnic sentience. In the hearings she brought in the research and records she had performed while under Ovewatch, alongside previous evidence used for Aurora's original case. In response to the mountains of undeniable evidence, the UN agreed and granted Omnic kind legal personhood status worldwide. In spite of this, not every government complied, and many humans would continue to resent and discriminate Omnic communities. Cases like Cliff Brassey, the first human charged for Omnic Murder, echo the feelings of many people around the world: "Breaking a machine is property damage, isn't it? This'll blow over. We'll put the tin cans back in the kitchen and forget this ever happened."
The road towards equality would be a long and dragged out one, but progress was possible, and more than welcomed.

On May 1st of 2060, Ye Wuyang was born. The younger of the Ye siblings, forever under his sister's shadow. Wuyang grew up seeking to meet his family's standards and would often train alongside his older sister in martial arts. While Anran was always outstanding, yet pressured to keep an eye on her younger brother, Wuyang tended to fall behind his sister, though they both aimed towards following the family's tradition and eventually getting accepted into Wuxing's Fire College.

While Overwatch's reputation and support was still high across the world, over the last couple of of years they have experienced a series of rejections. Korea refused the establishment of a Watchpoint: in Busan, then Numbani chose to remain outside of jurisdiction in spite of Doomfist's attacks. And many other things got in the way of operations around the world.

Reyes and Cassidy would begin a crackdown on criminals in Calgary, Chicago and Saint Paul. And during this time, a drug trafficker would raise a lawsuit in his defense, arguing Overwatch had no authority over living humans, only Omnics. Naturally, this was quickly dismissed and seen as an attempt to extort money and avoid prosecution, but the red tape and politics of it all slowed Overwatch down, and only continued to frustrate Reyes, who began to break protocol more often, keeping things to himself to avoid delays.

Not long after the Xie Incident, another similar overstep took place in Cape Town where a rouge God Program that escaped containment and rebel against its captors, caught the attention of Anubis loyalists and formed an insurrection. The same red tape that prevented Ana's deployment in Russia had now stopped Morrison from sending in any troops. Lucky for him, Lacroix had extensive covert ops training and came up with the idea of sending both him and Reyes "on vacation." The pair had a quiet trip, limiting themselves to intel gathering and evacuation of sources, as well as, on the rare occasion, the disappearance of one or two criminals. Coincidentally, their vacation led to the apprehension of the rouge AI and the loyalist suddenly vanished, all without official Overwatch involvement. Following this success and the repeated tension with international bureaucracy, Morrison would approve of more and more vacations between the Blackwatch staff, Cassidy joining them in many cases, but whether Jack knew the full extent of these trips is unknown.

Over the years, the Shimada family had come to rely on the Yamagami Blades, the business run by Toshiro and his wife, Asa. The Yamagami name has served the city for generations following traditional paths, heavily linked by the local shrine to the Fox Spirit, and now under Shimada control, the family chose their side in the turf war of the clans. Not only did Toshiro develop the Anima weapons used by the clean head and his sons, but his wife proved to be quite an asset as well. Often regarded as the best sword master in the world, Asa would serve as the teacher to the Shimada brothers. From a very young age, Asa wished for his daughter to also choose the path of the blade, so since she was very little, Kiriko would often join the brothers in training. Both brothers would quickly grow attached to the little girl, seeing her as a little niece figure. Genji in particular, was one to slack off from training and play with the kids, stealing sweets from the kitchen and playing games in the arcade.

 It was not just the brothers who Kiriko grew close to, since she spent so much time in the Shimada Castle, the clan leader, Sojiro Shimada had also grown accustomed to her presence. She would often join the family during the fireworks festivals at the end of summer, and during one night, he told his sons the stories of the clan. How centuries ago, a rival clan attempted to end their rule by setting the orchards aflame, but the Shimada did not move to defend the fields. Instead, they aided the people. These teachings heavily shaped Kiriko's perspective of the clan as Kanezaka's protectors, while she was still too young to understand the true nature of their operations.

On the off days when Kiriko was not training, she spent time at the Fox shrine with her grandmother, who taught her the traditional ways of spiritual cleansing and meditation. From an early age, her grandmother would teach him how to use the Anima ofuda that her dad had crafted, to summon the Fox spirit and use it to aid those in need. Much like how her mother wanted her to follow in her footsteps, her grandma had laid another path for her as well.

description.source: On December 21st of 2060, Illari Quispe Ruiz was born. As a child from Runasapi, Illari was surrounded by war heroes and a community that embraced Solar Threading technology, powering their entire city and defining their way of life. From a very early age, she decided to one day become one of the Inti Warriors, bowing to the desires of her community and dedicating her free time to training, so that one day she could live up to the legends that surrounded her.

"Dez" Stone would grow up in the living hell of the Australian Outback, where other exhiled savages roamed in caravans fighting in an unending battle for land and resources, in a hostile, radiated wasteland. If that was not enough already, wastlanders still needed to defend themselves from the Omnics, who had been forever changed by the radiation messing with their systems and the struggle to survive in harsh environments pushed them to become feral. Neither machines nor men were truly sane or safe. The Stones fought hard to survive this harsh life but one by one, they would fall all of them, except for Dez. Fueled by her anger towards King Mason for doing this to her family, and the loss of her loved ones, Odessa endured for years and became a formidable wasteland warrior, who scrapped Feral Omnics for parts to use on armor and weapons, including an electro magnetic gauntlet that proved deadly against anyone who opposed her. 

Years later, the memories of that day, where her family had vanished, still cause her nightmares.

Years had gone by and Shion still found herself captive by the Hashimoto, but over time she began to hold back, secretly pulling her punches and learning their weaknesses so that one day she could overtake them. Her captors were now revered amongst the Hashimoto. Calling themselves the elders and dressing up in traditional Japanese clothing. In their comfort at the top, they grew complacent, and began to lower their guards around Shion. This allowed Shion to take them by surprise, breaking free and taking on all four of the elders in a gruesome fight that left a trail of death, as the Omnic successfully murdered them all.

Shion was not only free at last, she also found herself as the new leader of the Hashimoto. All the humans who mistreated her for years now had no other option than to kneel and follow her every command, or risk becoming her next target. Having taken control of her fate, she chose four humans amongst those smart enough to bow to her power, and granted them seats at her new table of elders, at least as long as they remained useful and submissive, as they all knew very well how easily replaceable they truly were.

Lucheng's experiments with the Ape Colony had turned out fairly successful, and as the years went on, the animals began to develop unexpected side effects. Most notably, they grew in size and brain function. The team down on Earth was thrilled by the discovery and wished to experiment further to study any findings, but because of the funding of the Red Promise project, an already dangerous secret of theirs, spending more on such a morally questionable idea was risky, and far too expensive. To bypass the budget and moral concerns and keep the studies under the radar, Lucheng approved the use of hamsters as cheaper dispensable alternatives.

On October 15 of 2062, Specimen 8 would be born, and quickly experimented on like the rest of his siblings. Nicknamed "Hammond" by the researchers, he would quickly grow and surpass all their expectations of intelligence, completely overshadowing the rest of his siblings. Hammond to this day has memories of those early days of lonely enlightenment. The way his increased intelligence made it unable for his mother to communicate with him, how the scientists would bet on each of his siblings during every test, and how he hoped every time at least one of them would finally break through and join him. A painful existence under thoughtless Gods, where all he wished to do was escape.

The Martins had been some of Overwatch's most respected and valued members since the founding of the organization back during the Crisis. And within Overwatch, they have achieved massive accomplishments on a global scale after founding the Ecopoint program. However, the couple was not tied to the organization and in its later years they moved on from it to begin a project of their own.

After leaving Overwatch behind, the Martins formed The Collective. A scientific research nonprofit organization that could operate outside a politically regulated scope. It was meant to be a community made by scientists, for scientists, where every member contributed anything they could, and all of them shared the fruit of everyone's labor. This Utopic idea would later develop into the Atlantic Arcology, a massive sea spire made out of durovidro, that would become the home of the collective and anyone from the outer world who wished to be a part of their dream. Arcology became a self-sustaining, eco-friendly city that was not tethered to global politics, where scientists could continue their research without fears of funding or blockades, all with the objective of benefiting humanity as a whole. Many of the world's preeminent scholars and artists would end up sailing to the Spire, especially those seeking political asylum. As a result, it also went on to become a haven for Omnic refugees across the world, and the Collective welcomed them with open arms. Aside from the recurrent presence of curious whales migrating near the facilities and disrupting traffic in and out of the city, Arcology was a massive success for the scientific community, and showed many that Overwatch's goals could be pursued without their involvement.

Following the Crisis many Omnics struggled to integrate into human society. Very few of them managed to climb up the ladder of capitalism, but perhaps there is no bigger success than that of Maximillien. Before the crisis, Max was a low-level accountant in Marseille, but following the Awakening he found himself in the position of a preeminent financial advisor for La Coterie, the name the press had given to a group of Europe's most influential power brokers. While he was often stepped on by many of his clients, soon enough they all began kneeling at his feet.  For the longest time, his clients blindly trusted their assets into Max, and behind their backs he had built an elaborate web of money laundering and contingency agreements, very carefully worded deals that would all direct those fortunes directly to him. After years of serving ignorant, arrogant Tycoons, Max arranged a meeting with the six most powerful figures of Monaco, and broke to them the news; he owned each one of them and their companies. 

Overnight, Max had become one of the most powerful figures in out of Europe, and the head of La Coterie. The Omnic was one call away from bankrupting anyone he wished to, so his old clients had no real choice but to serve him. Over the years, Maximillien had guided the reconstruction and rise of Monte Carlo from the shadows, and after years of effort he owned half of the city. His reign over Monaco would continue to expand as he pursued other deals across Europe and beyond, later acquiring Don Rumbotico in Cuba and using it as yet another front for his money laundering. From the window views of his casino, Max watched as the world's wealthiest and powerful elites fed from his hand.

It had been ten years since the end of the Crisis, and Angela's early career was already a fruitful one. Her breakthroughs in the field of applied nanobiology radically improved the treatment of life-threatening injuries, capable of stabilizing near-death patients and saving countless lives. Through her schooling and early years outside of college, Overwatch kept an eye on her, allowing her access to the Watchpoints as she volunteered on the medical staff. Ziegler's technology could have made her rich if she chose to remain in private practice, but she always saw science as something that belonged to the world and the people who benefited from it.

It was here when Morrison finally chose to approach her directly. As the world finally moved away from the crisis, Morrison wished to shift towards peacetime and civilian applications. The heavy investment in the support departments and Ecopoint bases was one of the early signs of this new mission, making the world a better place. As such, Morrison offered Angela to become the leader of the medical division, with all the money, resources and personnel she could ever dream of. Angela was intrigued by these promises, but she was greatly opposed to the militaristic nature of Overwatch. Even since losing her parents to the war, she did not have the greatest opinion on military peacekeeping.

In the end, she had agreed to the offer with one caveat. The same way Torbjörn requested back in the day, she wanted to become a part of the strike team, so she could keep a level of control over the use of her technology and allow her to see at work personally. Morrison agreed. In order to work on the frontlines, she began development of the Valkyrie swift-response suit, a personal aerial combat armor that came equipped with nanobiotic capabilities and assistive protocols. Ziegler quickly proved to be a surprisingly adept field agent, with a surgical tactic approach to changing situations. Between her efficiency and the design of her suit, she quickly gained notoriety among the strike team, earning her the call sign "Mercy". While she did not enjoy the way this framed her, she was always glad to use her technology for the greater good.

Rumiko Shimada had left the clan years ago, vanishing mysteriously one night. Nobody knew what caused her to leave, but everyone assumed she couldn't live with the Yakuza lifestyle anymore. Her absence made Sojiro extremely protective of his sons, who were raised with the expectation of inheriting command of the Clan together.

Genji, however, had no interest in the clan. He had often thought of leaving as well, were it not for his brother and little Kiriko, who helped him keep a sense of belonging in Hanamura Castle. His disinterest led to developing a playboy lifestyle as a young adult, skipping important clan meetings and sword training to play video games at the local arcade, often taking Kiriko alongside him, though even when he didn't, she would sneak out and follow behind him.

His carelessness would fall on Hanzo, who got tangled in his brother's escapades far too often, and tended to cover for him when it came time to face their father. Hanzo wasn't too keen on inheriting the clan either, but being the older of the two, expectations were harder on him, and his father had less patience for him than he was for Genji. Hanzo wished that when the day came, he could rule the clan his way, with Genji as his equal, so he worked hard to share his discipline and guidance with him, but on the other hand, Genji was just waiting for the day they kicked him out, and the elders of the clan were getting tired of Sojiro's inability to control his own children.

Amélie Guillard had left her home years ago, tired of the aristocratic lifestyle that her family had attempted to impose on herself. Through her dancing skills, she pursued a career in Ballet that allowed her to gain notoriety, eventually becoming a prima ballerina known in all of France and abroad.

Her life would take a more interesting turn, however, when she met a certain diplomat in Paris. Gérard Lacroix, Blackwatch's second in command, is currently spearheading investigations into several criminal groups across the world. The pair had dated for a long time, with Amélie being present at Vivian's induction and becoming relatively known around many of the Strike team. Years later, they would go on to marry and live a pleasant life together, although it seemed some of Gérard's closest friends had their reservations with her. Jack Morrison, who had grown particularly close to Lacroix, warned him that something was wrong about her, but Gérard merely found it funny.

Amélie herself, however, gave little thought of her husband's career, as it mostly made for a conversation topic at parties in her eyes. However, her husband was one of the only things Amélie genuinely loved throughout her life, the only other thing she ever felt as passionate about being ballet.

With Angela leading the medical division, Overwatch began campaigns around the world using Nanobiotics to heal those in need, and perhaps there was no other place that needed it the most than Australia. Following the explosion of the Outback Omnium, the high amount of radioactive material blasted into the air and water led to a catastrophic health crisis in the region. While Ecopoint: Zealandia focused on helping the environment heal, the people of Australia needed help to get through the radiation poisoning faster. Cases escalated, and the cancer rate skyrocketed, and in spite of Australia's prior resistance to Overwatch action, Ziegler would not stand by such a tragedy.

Under Angela's command, a mission team would be deployed, comprised of nearly the entire medical staff, alongside Chase and Sarioglu, both rising stars in the Strike team, well versed in public relationships. Together, they collaborated with local governments and local nonprofit groups to help get resources to affected populations, and bring those in remote locations into the Melbourne hospital, where Ziegler could give intensive care. Thanks to their efforts, the projected mortality rate was cut by more than seventy percent, and a wing of the Melbourne hospital was renamed for Ziegler. As the team was ready to leave, a group of Junkers came out of the You Yang Mountains and attempted to claim the city of Little River, hoping to take the medical facilities for themselves once Overwatch left. Ziegler and Chase were still present when the attack happened and were able to repel the raiders with no lives lost. However, they chose to stay at their post and monitor for further hostilities, delaying their return for over a month.

Upon returning from Australia, Vivian would be surprised when she was dispatched to a smaller, though not less vital mission. She had been requested by a charity organization dedicated to creating memories for children in critical condition. Jada Levine, a twelve-year-old girl with a more aggressive case of the disease Vivian once had faced, was now moved to palliative care, and qualified for the organization's program. Her wish? You spend a day with Vivian Chase, the savior of Canada and her personal hero.

Vivian accepted, and two weeks later made the trip to Toronto, where the little kid was infatuated with Overwatch, and with Sojourn especially. The exact details of the meeting remain confidential and undocumented, except for Jada's own social media, filled with pictures of herself and her hero, during the last day of her life. Those pictures made the matter public, and Vivian came under fire for not bringing Mercy, the new team member hailed as a miracle worker, alongside her.  But Angela herself answered to this criticism, after getting permission from the parents to comment on her condition. The child was in a far too critical state, her condition too advanced, making surgeons unable to use cybernetics as an option to save her life. Nanobiotics as well had been taken to their extreme during the treatment. Even miracles have their limits. There was nothing Angela could have done, other than pull focus towards herself. Following this occasion, Chase became a far more vocal advocate for research into treatments for her disease, all the way through the end of her days in Overwatch.

While the Shambali faith aided hundreds of Omnics to find peace with themselves and the world, the threat of Omnic injustice still lingered, even way after the rulings in favor of personhood. Ramattra had found himself among the many monks who followed Tekhartha Mondatta's teachings, but he failed to see any progress in their vision. While the Shambali urged him to be patient, he could not stand the injustices that his people endured all around the world, without anyone taking action, and so on day, he decided to leave the temple, saying his farewells to his master, Mondatta and his closest friend, Zenyatta.

Ramattra wondered around the world and saw the horrors the Omnics lived through, not just discrimination and segregation, but many kidnapped and dismantled for parts, and those who lived relatively normal lives were forced into squalid conditions by ignorant humans who insisted they did not need sanitary measures, heat or water. In time, the brutal truth started to hit many Omnics. They were a one-generation species. Once they die, no more can be made. Their already limiting numbers were going down by resentful humans who could never understand what their lives were like, and so underground movements of angered Omnics began to appear. During his time in Europe, Ramattra would liberate many Omnics from forced servitude and begin to amass a following. While initially peaceful, this group stood in stark contrast to Mondatta's approach to coexistance; they were far more pro-active and resentful of humanity. This group would be known as Null Sector, a movement of Omnics that defy the numbers humans gave them, all zeroes, undefined.

Not long after the Gwishin attack, Overwatch received another emergency call from Busan. The Colossus had reappeared, larger than before and upgraded with new abilities. Overwatch dispatched all available agents, but even then, the tactics they used the previous time were no longer effective against it, and the team continued to struggle in maritime battles, so as the giant approached the coastline they were forced to evacuate the city. Fortunately, at the time, the strike team had grown rapidly, and new agents like Fusionator and Soundquake played a big role in defeating the Gwishin. The new agents had not faced the Gwishin before, yet their unique abilities proved effective when everything else failed. They were able to distract the colossus long enough for the rest of the team to take it down.

Mina Liao would be joined by Dr. Yi-am Lim, a robotics engineer from the Korean military. They both analyzed the footage and concluded the warbot was an upgraded version of that of the previous attack, but everyone wondered how that would be possible. It would require an entire team of the best engineers to get this machine running again after years, yet the timeline did not add up. Artificial Intelligence must have been involved in the accelerated development, and everyone began fearing the worst. Liao's research team was dispatched to the Temple of Anubis, to determine if the rouge AI had managed to escape containment, but they found no breaching happened. The researchers were astounded by trying to look for a source, when the third attack happened.

The colossus reemerged from the water, evolved yet again with a design that directly countered Soundquake's technology. Thanks to Dr Lim and yet another new agent, Rumble, the team was able to identify weak points and defeat the machine quicker, and with a smaller force this time. The swift response allowed Lim's team to retrieve the wreckage before the warbot dived back into the water. Thanks to this, they discovered the Gwishin had not been built in any known Omnium. Overwatch scouted the local sea floor and found a series of small drones lurking in the depths, attacking the diving team and forcing them to retreat. The only logical conclusion Liao could reach was that somewhere in the depths of the East China Sea, there was a secret Omnium, likely built by Anubis, and possibly it was not the only one. In spite of their combined efforts and Lim's wishes, Korea chose to remain independent in this battle, and Overwatch left after sharing their findings, despite Liao's frustration with the government choosing politics over allowing Overwatch to protect their people.

Doctor De Kuiper had dedicated decades of his life to the study of gravitational forces and how to harness their power. His research had reshaped the world with flying cars and connecting the entire planet with a transcontinental train, and yet, he continues to seek more. Years of research in The Hague led him to believe it would soon be possible to harness the power of a black hole. In order to test his theory, he would perform an experiment within the Interstellar Journey Space Station. Then everything went wrong. Something failed during the experiment, triggering the formation of a black hole for a brief, yet fatal moment. Siebren found himself right in the gravitational field of the experiment as the black hole appeared, and during this period of time he was exposed to its raw power. De Kuiper survived, both a miracle and a curse, as he now had to pay for the consequences of his hubris. The area nearing Dr. Siebren began to experience strange fluctuations in gravity, relative to his reactions to what was happening around him. To make matters worse, the experience left Siebren with serious psychological damage, incapable of acting coherently and mentioning a constant, maddening melody that nobody else heard. His distress caused the fluctuations to peak. He had to be evacuated immediately.

Just like his student before him, Tekhartha Mondatta would choose to leave the monastery not long after Ramattra did. While Ramattra sought to unify Omnics within a banner of justice and liberation, Mondatta believed the Shambali teachings could be used to teach equality and aid Omnic communities around the world through peaceful dialogue. In order to do this, Mondatta traveled the world, giving speeches and meeting with local authorities to discuss measures towards full Omnic Integration, and the place Mondatta had his eyes on to achieve the first milestone was King's Row, in London. 

The Omnics of England had been forced to live in the Underworld, a subterranean complex dug from abandoned Tube lines, power grid and sewage systems. Checkpoints around the city enforced curfews and police kept the Omnic people at bay to maintain segregation. This constant struggle had deemed London one of the main centers of Human Omnic tension in Europe, and the perfect spot for Mondatta to test his influence and teachings. Working with Major Mandah to begin work on Turing Green, a public housing development plan that would effectively give the Omnics a proper home, where they could live alongside human peers, without hiding underground. Mondatta's influence in the city could be felt within the Omnic community and with the groundbreaking of Turing Green, it marked the first step in rectifying years of injustice that Omnics had endured... if only it had lasted.

During her time as a prisoner, Shion rarely got very few, brief glimpses of the outside world. While Omnics across the world slowly developed their own culture and faith, Shion knew herself not as an Omnic, but instead as inhuman. She never had a chance to develop a sense of self, but now with all the money and power she could dream of, she had the means to transform herself into something she felt comfortable being. Shion performed heavy repairs and modifications to her chassis, mostly cosmetic, sculpting a shape that had an uncanny resemblance to that of a human, but yet she was still an Omnic, she belonged to no world other than the one she formed for herself.

Outside of her duties as head of the clan, Shion lived her life to the fullest, gaining a reputation for excessively indulging in all kinds of luxuries, from partying, costly fashion, plenty of lovers of both metal and flesh, and a growing love for custom-made holo bikes. Yet this carefree lifestyle didn't come in the way of her Hashimoto duties, in spite of what the other elders believed. While they comfortably sat in their chairs, Shion's craving for violence meant she was often working on the field with her men, doing most of the work for the clan, which only served to further secure her position as the most feared and influential of the Elders.

Upon returning to Earth, Doctor De Kuiper would be quarantined in a Secret Government facility somewhere in New Mexico. He was raving about the true nature of the universe, incoherently talking about time being non-linear, all while gravity around him shifted out of control. Once the most celebrated scientists in human history, Siebren found himself unable to hold reality together, and was deemed a danger to himself, and the world as a whole. 

For years, he would be detained under the name of "Subject: Sigma", in an isolated room where his power could be contained. As years went on, the Doctor retreated into his own mind and the forbidden knowledge that had now cursed him was his only company. For years, he thought he would never see the outside world again, and that whole time, that constant, eerie melody ringed in his ear.

Coppenhagen was hit by the crisis when Freja was only a child. Her mother was a diplomet at the time, and because of that everyone looked at her for answers. She commanded several operations right at the eye of the storm, calm constant and consistent, and through her Freja learned that keeping people safe came down to a level head and a focused eye. 

She had admired her mother's work for the longest time, but instead of following in her footsteps, she wished to save people on the ground alongside other operatives, placing herself in the middle of the storm. Following the Freja would go to University to pursue a criminology degree, granting her access to the latest tech available and how to identify and stop a threat before it even began, and outside of her classes she had joined her local search and rescue team to gain experience in the field. 

It was here where she developed outstanding skills at tracking down anyone, in any place, as she felt in love with the rush of seeing a job through the end, and making a difference hands on. For the longest time, Freja dedicated herself to chasing that gratifying feeling, of doing something that mattered and being good at it. Her determination and skil would soon open many doors for her.

The Vishkar Empire was ever-growing, especially after the success of the Architech Academy. Although power stayed relatively within the family of the late founder, it would be more accurate to compare the company to a dynasty. Vaira Singhania was the granddaughter of Vishwakarma Bhatt himself, and as such she was expected to one day inherit the business for herself. From a very young age, she struggled to form coherent structures with Hard Light, mostly making organic, ill-defined shapes, and while she liked to consider them art, her family disagreed. All she saw from their eyes was disappointment, and this pressure quickly shaped her into a perfectionist, and someone very insecure about her own merits.

 As she grew older she developed a knack for corporate politics, excelling in all types of lessons from debates and economics, truly a woman shaped to lead a business as large as her family's. And yet, she still lacked the artistic eye needed to perfect Hard Light manipulation, a harsh truth that cut through her, especially with the opening of the academy. As young students graduated to become leading engineers, it became clear that Vaira, the future head of the company, was falling behind her future employees. Yet Vaira did not give up. She worked tirelessly to shape her reputation within the company, spending a fortune on a pair of Mag Lev mechanical arms, capable of manipulating Hard Light just as an architect would. Through this assistive design, she was able to compete against regular architects and come off as an effortless, naturally gifted professional. As Vaira mascaraded through her education, she slowly moved up the corporate ladder outside Vishkar. She insisted on taking on the challenge outside the family business, working on private equity to perfect her own negotiation skills and reinforce her public image, so that once she returned, she would be seen as worthy of taking the family mantle.

As the Scourge of Numbani continues its rampage across the city. Numbani would choose to remain independent, in spite of Overwatch's efforts to assist with the problem from the outside. To counter the warmonger's attacks, the city funded the creation of an early warning system, as well as the upgrading and reprogramming of a squadron of OR14 Idina line warbots. The reborn OR15 security robots would serve as the city's primary defense to external threats and oppose Doomfist's incursions into the city, to mixed results. 

Between Numbani's own defense force and Overwatch dismantling his lieutenants on the outside, Adeyemi found himself looking for more mercenaries to bolster his ranks. Among these new recruits came in Akande Ogundimu, the heir of Ogundimu Industries. Akande had lost his right arm during the crisis, and while his company provided him with cybernetics, the prosthetics deemed him to have an unfair advantage in martial arts competitions, forcing him to retire from fighting. Following the injury, Ogundimu grew into a bitter man who blamed the world for refusing him to participate in the sport he loved, and so he would come across Adeyemi, who offered him a place with his lieutenants. Akande was wary, but intrigued by learning more about the Doomfist's gauntlet and his connections to a shadow group of benefactors, going by the name of Talon.

Every few seasons, Junketown hosts the Reckoning. A week-long festivity where junkers from all the outback could feast endlessly, and take part in brawls and shows of strength. The main event of the Reckoning consisted of a free for all in the Scrapyard. A battle for the death in which challengers use all sorts of gadgets and machinery to gain an open hand. Anyone may publicly challenge the reigning monarch to a battle for the crown, provided they were the last man standing in the brawl.

King Mason had gone undefeated for several years, reigning as a tyrant and stomping over allies. The heads of each Junker faction had long tried to dethrone him and take the crown for themselves, but they would all be eclipsed by a certain newcomer. Odessa Stone, an exiled wastelander, made her way into the city and challenged Mason. In her recounting debut, she faced Mari of the Thinkers and Geiger of the Scavengers, and was able to tear through both, while still showing them mercy. Odessa valued connections and loyalty, and could tell the faction leaders did not support their King. As such, she wished to show all Junkers the kind of leader she could be. The match was also being broadcast across the Outback, which she counted on to gain clout and respect with the masses. After defeating all the contenders, Mason himself came down from the top of the scrapyard to take on the wastelander.

After a fierce battle that followed pushed Mason into a corner, as his true colors showed at his worst when he activated the Scrapyard's Magnetism in a desperate move to end the fight. As the crowd turned on Mason for his recklessness, the leaders took Odessa's side, since she spared both. With the magnet down, Odessa was able to defeat the King, and win over support from the crowd, becoming the new Queen of the Junkers.

description.source:
After Liao's work in Busan, she retreated back to Overwatch's research facility in Oslo. Years of work with Overwatch had slowly allowed her to gain support and leniency to work on her passion through passion, Artificial Intelligence. Following the success of the Athena AI, Liao would go on to work on several more complex projects in secrecy. Documentation on the rest of the projects following Athena is heavily classified, but we do know of her fifth and last, Project: Echo.

On February 5th of 2065, Project Echo went online for the first time. Her masterpiece, her legacy, her redemption, her apology all packaged into a perfect machine. Liao dreamed of one day improving on the design of Omnics, and possibly even replicating Aurora's sentience for years, but even after proving herself, Overwatch limited her research. In the end, Echo was designed as a multi-role adaptive robot that could learn by replicating behavior, using a chassis with Hard light projectors that would allow Echo to duplicate the form of those she scanned, not just learning from their behavior but imitating them to a T. In the end, what was supposed to push the boundaries of sentience once more, was decimated into yet another tool for Overwatch to deploy in missions.

Among the Apes in the Lunar Colony, one of the gorillas was displaying rapid brain development faster than the rest. Specimen 28, was taken under the wing of Dr. Harold Winston, who took care of the Gorilla almost like a son, nourishing his curiosity with science and tales of human ingenuity back on earth. The young gorilla spent his days assisting the Doctor on experiments, away from the other apes, as he had become an outcast among the other apes. At one point, 28 would be visited by a peculiar, small intruder. Specimen 8, Hammond, had escaped through the vents, and he had just interrupted his plans.

Not long before they first met, Hammond realized that Winston was just like him, another survivor of the genetic therapy who was showing intelligence faster than his peers, and he was struck with a sense of sympathy, at seeing someone just as alone as he was. He was moved by the ape's innocence and sense of wonder, and the two quickly became friends. During his nightly escapades, Hammond would sneak treats like candy and peanut butter, and aid the gorilla in fixing things that the others break. In return, the ape showed him how to dream of a better life. The pair spent hours watching the giant blue marble just outside the window of the habitat, wondering what awaited them there. 

The pair wished to one day leave the base together and explore this distant world, and it just so happened that Hammond's escapades were not just to visit his friend. All this time, he had been tinkering with nuts and bolts, learning how the machinery in the base work, and he quickly fancied himself a mechanic. Even if the scientists found him every time he escaped his cell, none of them had a clue about the real purpose of his exploration of the base. He was set on leaving the moon, and taking Specimen 28 with him.

After years of pushback from many governments, and seeing the sucess of their continous "vacations" Reyes approached Morrison with the idea of expanding his division to deal with more questionable operations, taking care of things outside of the protocol and away from the public eye. With Morrion's approval, Blackwatch as we know it, was born. The small cover up division Reyes had been running expanded into a midsize initiative, expanding with several bases and gaining recruitment under Amari's selection. During these hirings, many people who would have otherwise not passed Overwatch's regular screenings would go on to become part of Reyes' staff, often kept secret from Ana and Jack. Perhaps the most well known of these fringe hires was Genji Shimada.

Overwatch was keeping an eye on the Shimada clan for years, but their influence in the Kanezaka region made them hard to take down legally. That was until the assassination of the clan leader, Sojiro Shimada, at the hands of a rival gang, the Hashimoto. Ever since his death, the clan began to expand its criminal activities, and their carelessness marked them as a target for Overwatch to take down. During initial scouting and intel gathering, Ziegler and Sarioglu were notified of a man who had been critically injured. The man turned out to be Genji Shimada, heir to the clan, and was taken into Overwatch's care as a potential valuable source of information.

Following his father's death, the elders of the clan took control and began to put pressure on his older brother, Hanzo, to take control as the new leader. For the longest time, Genji took little interest in the illegal activities of the clan so the elders considered him a liability and resented Sojiro's softness, so when Hanzo took control of the clan, they instructed him to straighten up his own brother. Genji refused, and tensions grew between the two brothers, building to a violent confrontation with a blade which left Genji on the verge of death.

With Overwatch expanding all of its departments from Blackwatch to the Ecopoint program, Ana Amari aided each division in the recruitment process and one. Generally, most of the supportive staff tended to be overshadowed by the Strike team in the public eye, but one key addition gained notoriety even among the Strike team itself: Freja Skov, the so called best tracker in the world.

At the time Freja had made a name for herself publicly working as a part of local search and rescue teams. The milirary wanted to hire her after her graduation from University but she always had her eye on  bigger fish. Ana Amari approached Freja to join a burgeoning search and rescue division among the Overwatch support personnel.

While in Overwatch, Freja would quickly gain notoriety for her unmatched excellence on the job, with many considering her the best tracker in the world. Freja would go on to become personally requested as an assiting operative by several members of the Strike team, like Reinhardt, Mercy and particularly Emre Sarioglu, who she grew especially close with, often taking trips to Istanbul together while on break from duty. For Freja, while the rest of the Strike team was often unreachable, super humans, Emre felt like any other guy, and he always made time to bond with people of all divisions, not just Search and Rescue.

Mizuki's home life continues to deteriorate, as misfortune continued to haunt the family. Dead after death had taken a toll on Mizuki's father as he felt further into superstitions and scams. Failing to cope with the tragedies that marked his life, he continued to blame it on malevolent spirits, and taught his child to fear them. In an attempt to escape their curse, the two would move out of Fukuoka and into Tokyo, but as his father's mental state continued to worsen, he would begin to accumulate debt from the many scams, lucky charms and exorcists that he had paid for as a desperate attempt to ward off the ghouls. Mizuki's father would begin to take loans from the Hashimoto Clan, the local criminal group who called Tokyo their home turf. 

As the family plunged further into debt, Mizuki could only watch in fear, until the day his father was found dead, leaving him to fend for himself. At only nine years old, Mizuki was left as an orphan, and inherited mountains' worth of debt to the Hashimoto. The young kid had internalized the years' worth of trauma that his father inflicted upon the family, so he believed the curse would claim his own life next. As the Hashimoto barged in to collect the debts, one of the Elders would take a keen interest in the young boy. Lady Shion showed Mizuki mercy by forgiving his debt if he joined their organization under her watch, where she would train him and teach him the ways of the clan. Without nowhere else to go, Mizuki accepted this fate reluctantly.

Null Sector activity continued across the world, inspiring many Omnics to follow Ramattra's teachings, especially following the groundbreaking of Turing Green, which many followers of Mondatta saw as a new start for Omnics. Null Sector, in contrast, took the idea as an insult, throwing a bone at his people to try and act like it absolved them from years worth of injustice. As momentum grew, the group radicalized from a small cell of liberators, to a fully militarized operation. The escalation meant many of his initial supporters soon began to leave the group behind, but his resolve to bring justice for all Omnics only grew stronger with each ally he lost.

He decided to bring his closest allies, Nameless, Zera and Lanet, on a journey across the depths of a freezing wasteland, where they found the very same Anubis made Omnium, where Ramattra was born. His plan was to use the facility to create an army, and use it to speak to humans in a language they can understand, violence. For the next two years, the group would produce entire battalions of Crisis-era units at Lanet's supervision, and Ramattra himself would upgrade his own design combining Shambali technology with an invention of his own, Nanites, microscopic machines capable of cooperation and assembly of different structures, including extra reinforced limbs for close combat. As his army grew, Ramattra already had his eyes on the first target of his revolution, but Lanet urged caution, noting the antiquated designs needed more work if they wanted to get things right.

During this back-and-forward, tension built up over philosophical differences amongst the group, as Ramattra continuously refused to involve other Omnics and rally forces outside his mindless troops. While Nameless and Zera were used to appealing to the Omnic masses, and wished to allow their people to fight alongside them, Ramattra was tired of bloodshed. He saw himself as a liberator, not a general. It was because of this that he chose to manufacture an army of robots, instead of using his influence to command his supporters, as he wished to keep sentient Omnics away from active conflict as much as possible. This led to constant argument with his allies, who saw their leader radicalize further into a lonely crusade.

After hearing his story, Gabriel Reyes pitched him the idea of joining forces. If Genji agreed to work with Blackwatch to take down the rest of the Clan, Overwatch could rebuild his body with cybernetics. Angela Ziegler, the head of the medical division and the one in charge of Genji's care, objected to the coercion of his patient, but Genji, enraged by what his brother had done and without much of a choice in his mutilated state, accepted the offer. 

Ziegler was opposed to the procedure, worrying about the weaponizing of the augmentations she would need to develop for Genji, but ultimately committed when given the direct order to do so. With the full scope of the medical team, Ziegler replaced the man's falling organs with cybernetics, mostly based on the ones Sojourn herself relied on. 

Once he was stable, they began to augment his body and turned him into a living weapon. Genji and Angela formed a very close bond over the several months that passed during the procedure, and this connection was pivotal in Genji's future reassignment to the strike team.

As Niran grew older, he would use his parent's wealth to travel the world during his breaks from the architecture academy. While exploring the wilderness of the globe, he was able to experience the turmoil that existed in the world outside his bubble of wealth. Animals and forests dying, in part due to Vishkar's own expansion, war, illness and poverty everywhere he looked, with people who needed help being actively ignored, entire communities riddled with pain. 

Niran became determined to use his talents to fix the world, and began to experiment with healing applications of hardlight. After months of research at the Architech Academy, Niran used his knowledge and fascination of botany. Niran would push the limits of hardlight design into something new entirely. A self-replicating biomass made from hardlight. A living, organic material manifested from light structures, capable of repairing tissue near its light in the blink of an eye. Biolight was a revolutionary discovery that could change the world and bring balance back between man and nature. However, he would soon discover that was not possible under Vishkar.

For years, Akande Ogundimu had trained under the wing of Akinjide Adeyemi, as one of the best lieutenants. His involvement was known by Numbani's security forces, but he was smart enough to keep distance away from more active conflicts to avoid being apprehended. As Ogundimu became one of Adeyemi's most trusted confidants, behind his back, Akande was thinking far bigger than he could ever have imagined. Akande was a well-studied visionary, who had grown to adopt a certain philosophy as his personal mantra: Humanity evolves through conflict.  =It was conflict like the pandemics earlier in the century that pushed medical advances to their limits. It was conflict like the ecological impact of humanity that led to the hundreds of inventions that made life better. It was a conflict like the Omnic Crisis that allowed humanity to come together with Overwatch, and push through an enemy larger than any nation on their own. It was conflict that prevented him from sports, and allowed him to realize his true calling. Akande was meant to spread conflict across the world, for the betterment of humanity.

Akande had grown connections within Talon's council through Adeyemi's network of mercenaries, and within the council they saw him as a potentially valuable asset. Before long, Ogundimu made his choice. He turned against his master and after a brutal face off, he was able to kill him, taking the Gauntlet and the mantle of Doomfist for himself. Akande was already respected within Talon, but between his vision, and now the imposing force of the Gauntlet, the members of the council would have little option but to fall in line at his command. After all, it would be easier to take advantage of governments and industry amid the chaos of ongoing conflicts, so while the new Doomfist pursued an ideology, his closest allies stuck around purely to profit from his crusade.

Under Doomfist, Talon would shift from being an amorphous, silent force that hijacked power across regions, to a loud, imposing terrorist that quickly proved to be Overwatch's primary obstacle in their peacekeeping duties. The organization was actively growing at this time as well. Research teams began to raise warnings of fringe scientists being recruited by Talon agents, and in some cases, reputable researchers getting kidnapped. Perhaps a more direct blow would be the beggining of a recruitment campaign across the Carribean Sea, as many experienced personnel from the Caribbean Coalition ranks began to be lured by the calling of Talon. Reyes and Lacroix became aware of the change in leadership and even obtained partial footage of the battle. The subject became a main priority for their research, but soon enough, Overwatch would have their hands full from dealing with Talon.

Overwatch's research team was relatively quieter than the many controversies the Strike team and Blackwatch would eventually be remembered for, but one of their many experiments would become one of the things the organization became the most known for. Lena Oxton was at the time a young pilot in the Brittish Royal Air Force and had just enlisted into Overwatch for trials of their next generation, teleporting fighter jet, the Splitstream. Lena might have been pretty young at the time, but her uniquely fast reflexes, hand coordination and love for flying at high speeds made her the most suited choice for the test that Britain could offer. 

Unfortunately, during the first test flight, the ship's teleportation matrix would malfunction, and suddenly both Oxton and the jet vanished. Lena was presumed dead, and the incident did not bring any good publicity for Overwatch, but what the scientists did not expect at the time was that Lena's disappearance was a far more complex, rare event than merely vanishing in the accident.

Oxton's molecular structure had become desynchronized from the regular flow of time and space, a condition that would later be called "Chronal Disassociation." In short, Lena was a living ghost, disappearing for hours and days at a time, and whenever she was visible in our present, it was often at completely different places, and she could barely maintain a physical form for long. Lena would remain in this limbo state for about two whole years, in which her body showed no signs of aging while disassociated from our timeline. After her first reappearance in the months after the accident, Shira Wexler, the lead designer of the jet, took full responsibility for her condition and dedicated her team's efforts to finding a cure.

After months of treatment, Genji's body was fully reconstructed, and the man had turned into a living weapon, filled with rage and eager to take down his family's business. Taking down the Shimada, a group so deeply rooted in the local community's culture and politics, required a stealth operation that only Blackwatch could see through the end, and with Genji's intel, they would be able to get the upper hand. After months of preparation, Reyes, Lacroix, Genji and Cassidy strategized strikes to arrest several of the major players left in the clan, disrupting their operations piece by piece until the entire Empire began crumbling from within. 

To make matters easier, the Clan had also lost their other heir, not long after Genji. Hanzo Shimada had abandoned his duties, feeling ashamed by his actions, since, as far as he knew, he had killed his brother in cold blood at the orders of a bunch of old men who were supposed to serve him. They say the man became a vagabond, taking his father's Anima storm bow with him as a memento, he swore never to wield a blade again, and once he left Hanamura Castle and began to travel the world, seeking for ways to restore his honor and put his old life behind.

 Without solid leadership, the remaining members of the clan began turning on each other and resorting to more openly illegal activities like blackmailing schemes, which slowly fractured their reputation with the Kanezaka community, fueling their decline further. The long-lasting Shimada Clan had been completely dismantled from the shadows, and although Genji craved more, and actively pursued the take-down of other rival gangs in the region like the Hashimoto, the conditions that allowed for the fall of the Shimada were ultimately too circumstantial. Overwatch would not be as lucky as they were here if they tried to take on some of the bigger clans of the broader Tokyo region.

After Genji's recruitment into Blackwatch, Angela began to file many complaints against Reyes, stating that his actions went against everything that Overwatch stood for. Vivian was also openly opposed to Blackwatch, though given her special ops background, she showed more appreciation towards Reyes and what he could accomplish, just less about the extralegal nature of his actions. While Morrison noted these complaints and asked Reyes to avoid antagonizing them further, Reyes immediately prioritized finding a new medical official to specialize in Blackwatch operations. He came across a research paper released by an ambitious geneticist, Moira O'Deorain, DNA alteration at a cellular level. The methodology shared a lot of principles with the Soldier Enhancement Program, but innovated on them by making some morally questionable choices, where the treatment would cause cells to continually tear themselves apart and immediately regenerate, degenerating and repairing the subject's entire body on a constant loop.

Reyes flagged Moira as worth watching, but not long after, a condemnation by the medical staff was released, before he could run her credentials. Moira's work was problematic in the scientific community, with plenty of researchers unable to replicate the results, and the ethical shortfalls of her work resulted in growing dissent among her peers. This was not the promising step forward in human potential she had promised; it was mere shoddy science. Moira was dismissed from the University of Dublin, seen as a liability, and when she attempted to work in the private sector, her name had been blacklisted and no reputable group would employ her. Through all this, Ziegler specifically spoke out against O'Deorain, and Reyes ignored each and every remark.

Shortly after O'Deorain's recruitment, Overwatch would face a devastating loss in Ecopoint: Antartica. The scientific team on the base dedicated their studies to finding and replicating anomalous weather conditions, but not even with their equipment and knowledge were they able to foresee the quick formation of a massive superstorm in the region. Their experimentation with a prototype machine capable of simulating abnormal weather seemignly influenced the formation of a huge blizzard trapped the team within the base in unlivable conditions, and made evacuation efforts extremely risky. The Ecopoint facilities were equipped with cryo sleep technology, allowing the team to freeze their bodies and enter a stasis, which should have allowed them to survive until the storm passed. These kinds of storms had happened before, and it had become standard procedure, but this particular blizzard was worse than any projections could have estimated.

Veterans Captain Opara, Dr. Arrhenius, Dr. Adams and young Dr. Torres, Dr. MacReady, Dr. Mei-Ling Zhou were the team stationed at the time. As the storm raged on, the team remained in cryo-stasis, getting past the survival time window, where the system should have forced them to wake up, in the middle of the never-ending blizzard. Months passed, and the storm did not dissipate. Any attempts to establish communication failed, so the team was presumed dead. Overwatch would attempt to retrieve their bodies on multiple occasions, but the storm's anomalous persistence prevented access to the base for a full year. 


During one of the many rescue attempts, an Icebreaker ship, the Resolute, would crash into the Ice, and the rescue team barely managed to escape with their lives. The anomaly continued and Overwatch was forced to stop further retrieval attempts, lest they lose more agents. All of Overwatch entered a mourning period, with the Ecopoint bases rushing to improve security protocols in case of evacuation, and the UN calling for a full accounting of the records for review. Hector and Claudio joined their old partners in mourning the loss of the entire Antarctica team, and those who died trying to get their bodies back.

Soon after his takeover of Talon, Doomfist began his campaign of conflict by arranging a series of attacks on powerful figures across the globe. Maximillien, the head of the ever-growing Monte Carlo, was naturally a tantalizing target. The first assassin sent his way caused concern, but swiftly dealt with by his security staff. When the second assassin came, this was more flattering. Following this second attempt, the assassin would not return to Doomfist empty-handed, as they claimed the target proposed a deal. 

Not long after, Max found himself in the wreckage of his office, as the imposing figure of Doomfist himself towered over him. Max understood well the level of power he was dealing with, Doomfist was unquestioned and his crusade would not be stopped. All he could do if he had any hope of surviving, was join his side. Maximillien's deal allowed Akande access to his resources, money and connections, as well as his ability to manage Talon's assets effectively. In return, he asked to be allowed to live, as one of his council members. Talon's aid would also allow Maximilien to pursue more contentious negotiations, offering leverage through brute force.

Lucky for Maximillien, Doomfist respected his perseverance, his confidence and his ability to adapt, the deal was made, and Max dragged all of Monte Carlo into Talon's umbrella, just to save his own life. The deal, however, was still a losing hand for Max. At La Coterie, control was everything, and Max had long enjoyed being the one pulling the strings of everyone who was once above him. The house always wins, but if Talon took the house, what would be left of him?

In spite of all the warnings and advice of the medical staff in Overwatch, Gabriel sent an offer to Moira, promising resources, staff and a laboratory of her own, and while initially suspicious, the idea of rubbing her success in the faces of those who destroyed her career lured her in. Her employment was kept under absolute secrecy, and unlike most other Blackwatch agents, she was not openly associated with Overwatch's primary organization. If Blackwatch was Overwatch's dirty little secret, Moira was theirs.

Moira worked in the shadows, developing new weapons and technology for Blackwatch, even testing her genetic research on Gabriel himself. Since he was a SEP subject, it allowed her to further her progress by emulating the original formula. Experiments on Reyes lead to a monumental leap in Moira's research, allowing his body to continually repair itself, cheating death through sheer biological will. Despite this, however, the degeneration of tissue was quite volatile, and Reyes would begin to see his body tearing itself apart into smoke, before stabilizing itself back into shape, in an extremely painful, irreparable state of limbo. Moira herself would go on to apply the same experiments on her own body as well, and while Reyes did not exactly come out of the lab in good condition, this new ability proved useful in many Blackwatch missions that followed.

A growing anti-government sentiment began to spread around Mexico following the creation and expansion of Lumérico, as many believed that the reconstruction primarily benefited the rich and influential, while those who needed help the most were left behind.

After years of Energy Equity under the beloved Xibalba program, Lumérico's lack of commitment to upholding the lead to resentment among the people, and gave birth to Los Muertos.
A criminal group labeling themselves after the millions that died during the dark days of the Crisis, left behind by their own Government. One of their strongest assets was, surprisingly enough, a young girl.

Olivia Colomar was one of many left orphaned by the Crisis, and she endured the dark days alone in the cold, and with much of the country's infrastructure gone after the Crisis, she survived through a natural gift for computer programming, learning how to hack her way through any system to get by. When los Muertos took her underneath their wing, she welcomed them and even began to assist using her unique skills. Thanks to Olivia los Muertos, was able to get multiple hits against Lumérico and the government as a whole, and nobody in her community really suspected the nice little girl to be robbing them right under their noses.

During his research at the Academy, he would come to discover the notes of Vishwakarma Bhatt, the late founder of the corporation, as well as his dream of providing hardlight freely to the world. Niran wished Biolight would remain accessible to all as well, but seeing how quick the company was to ignore their founder's wishes, choosing to place restrictions on the technology and profit from their monopoly, Niran knew the same fate would await his discovery. 

When he unveiled the Biolight technology, Vishkar began to claim full ownership of the invention, and Niran resisted. Against the demands of Vishkar's higher ups and the advice of his closest friend Satya, Niran fled the academy and took his research on Biolight with him. Overnight, he became a wanted man on a crusade against a powerful empire, and to make matters worse, his family would cut him off from their wealth to pressure him into turning in his discovery. 

Niran was alone and hunted, but not out of options. He pleaded for sanctuary in the Atlantic Arcology, where he would be received by a supportive community of like-minded individuals. The nature of the Collective placed him outside global laws and prevented Vishkar from pursuing him further, and the assets of the Arcology allowed Niran to continue his research independently, working alongside the other members of the collective to bring his power to the world, free of charge.

Overwatch had taken down the Shimada clan, but in doing so it merely caused a power vacuum in the Kanezaka region. The illegal activities were not the only priority of the clan, as they also saw themselves as the protectors of Kanezaka for generations. In the words of their late leader, if the relationship the clan has with the people of the region is anything less than mutually beneficial, they were nothing more than a parasite. This social contract had stood strong for generations, as the Shimada kept larger, more dangerous gangs at bay, but as their empire crumbled and their operations became more openly shady, the people turned their backs on them, only to soon realize they were the lesser of two evils.

The Hashimoto clan had long been the main rival crime family to the Shimada, and after Overwatch left, they began a takeover of Kanezaka, placing Keigo Kuroura in charge of overseeing the region. As a stronger, more stable group, Overwatch did not have the same level of leverage against them that they did with the Shimada, so they were essentially able to reign uncontested. 

In spite of this, however, the Hashimoto quickly realized there was one potential threat lingering after the fall of the Shimada, the Yamagami Blades, particularly Toshiro himself, who was responsible for the powerful weaponry that allowed the Shimada to hold their ground for so long. The clan act quickly, kidnapping Toshiro and forcing him to supply their syndicate with Anima weapons of their own. Alone and with her hands tied, Asa saw no other choice but to send Kiriko away, changing her last name to Kamori, Asa's birth name, and taking her to live with her grandmother to protect her from the clan.
