description.source:
While the Ecopoints helped alleviate ecological concerns across the globe, not every nation was too keen on pushing environmentalist standards. Both corporate greed and sometimes even plain irresponsibility by well-meaning people got in the way. The super coral had successfully helped rejuvenate several coral trees across the Pacific, but it was far too effective. It kept expanding across the world's oceans, and as they continued to feed off of pollutants, they began to grow out of proportion, emerging out of the water into sharp structures comparable to small islands.

For many nations, these super coral reefs serve as another source of tourism and national pride, obvious to the true implications of an introduced species becoming so dominant. For businesses across the globe, however, the reefs blocked trade routes and made it difficult for boats to navigate across many different regions of the planet, disrupting trade globally. Because of their impact, many companies began to equip boats with means to break through the reefs, and some of the people of the Polynesian nations took to this as a personal insult to their culture and history. 

The Deep-sea Raiders came to call themselves activists who battled capitalism and took curving fossil fuel emissions into their own hands, but in reality they were little more than Eco-terrorists. The pirates would hijack many boats crossing near their territories, kill the tribulation, and then steer the ships to crash into the coral which would feed off the oil and debris, growing even larger than they would normally. The Polynesian League was naturally directly impacted by the Deep-sea Raider activity, which disrupted the ecological balance and worsened business relationships with other nations. The league sought to deal with these raiding cells swiftly, but they proved to be quite a persistent movement, supported by a lot of locals who saw this as the government turning back on their culture and the wishes of their people, in spite of the irreparable damage that their harsh actions caused.

After the Shimada takedown, Cassidy had been reassigned outside of Blackwatch, to temporarily run security at the Oslo laboratories, guarding Project: Echo. His status as a cover agent and Liao's own worries with Overwatch made her wary of him at first, but at the same time she was a fierce opponent of pigeonholder, and judging people via a checklist. With time she saw through Cassidy's cowboy persona, and got to meeth im for the funny, loyal, and clever man that he was, what is more he was willing to keep Liao's research and the extend of Echo's intelligence as a secret between the two of them.

When Echo was on her early stashes, she began to rech out to personnel, seeking additional input, this is how she first approached Cassidy, who interacted with her as if she were a fully fleshed person. Liao noted in her records that one time during Testing, Echo eliminated the wrong target and exhibited signs of distress, only for Cassidy to descalate the situation, reassuring her that everyone made mistakes, but what mattered is how they made their way through the world. 

This lead to Echo and Cassidy stablishing conversation and exchanging jokes, causing Echo to laugh for the first time. Cassidy's casual approach changed Liao's views on Echo, which sped up development now that she began to see her less as an apology for what happened with Aurora, and more like a child like intelligence that needed guidance to improve.

The Crisis left behind a broken world, and with it priceless history and icons of cultural value were lost. While many cities rebuilt themselves and archen back to the classical periods, it became all the more evident to many across the world how important it was to preserve history, what was left of it anyway. This is how the Wayfinder Society came to be, a group of archeologists and historians from around the globe, coming together to share resources and connections, all with the goal of preparing expeditions all over the world, to retrieve artifacts and find clues from the past to use in the present.

Sloan Cameron had spent their life traveling with their family, getting to see all corners of the world and exploring their culture and history each time they arrived at a new place. This innate curiosity as well as a keen eye for finding unearthed trinkets drew them to the Wayfinders. At age sixteen, they began an apprenticeship with the group, and never looked back. Sloan would adopt the nickname "Venture" while operating in digsites, and as they joined expeditions through ancient ruins and dormant Omniums, their unfettered bravery and persistence in dangerous situations would make them stand out among many other Wayfinders. Sloan would often return from dig sites covered in dirt, bruises and local fauna, but always with a smile on their face, and it was this passion and dedication that allowed them to take increasingly dangerous and exciting expeditions with the Wayfinders.

The Horizon Lunar Colony had stood strong for decades, it saw a changing world, survived the Crisis, and now was home to a generation of increasingly smarter Apes. The experiments pursued by the Horizon team, however, were extremely morally dubious in nature, and the animals themselves grew to resent their handlers for their actions. By this time, Dr. Chao, the head of the research, had returned to Earth, as long-term activity on the moon turned her bones feeble, unable to walk on land, or to get cybernetics, she had moved back to Lijiang Tower's administrative sectors, but the experiments continued without her, and the researchers soon would realize the price for crossing such ethical barriers.

Communication with Horizon was lost abruptly and never restored. What little is known is that the Apes ead an uprising against the staff, killing every single scientist, and claiming control of the colony for themselves. Specimen 28, a gorilla who grew attached to his caretaker, Harold Winston, saw his world crumble apart as his peers killed his teacher. 28 took his mentor's name into his memory and did what he could to find a way to escape the rioting of the other Apes, not knowing somewhere in the Colony, his old friend Hammond was one step head of him.

While he was a hostage, Toshiro had not yet surrendered himself fully to the Hashimoto. The man would agree to their demands for Anima weapons to keep himself alive, but he purposely butchered his own work, producing dismal blades with unstable Anima fields, effectively declawing the wielders from the potential danger they could pose.  The clan took notice of the poor quality of his work, so Lady Shion decided to use her pupil as leverage. 

Mizuki was still too young and weak to take part in criminal activities, but Shion believed that Toshiro might pick up the slack if the boy was endangered. With the life of a child on the line, Toshiro began to produce Animas of better quality, including a unique pair of pistols for Shion's personal use. Even if these powerful weapons paled in comparison with the mystifying Shimada Dragons or the Fox Spirit, at least in the eyes of the Elders, they measured up, and if they ever faltered, Shion could always threaten Mizuki again to make sure Toshiro cooperated.

Mizuki kept Toshiro company, and in return, Toshiro's kindness was able to balance his harsh walk of life as he got older and began to take part in clan duties. But on the other hand, Shion's discipline was unforgiving. The Omnic would often seriously injure the boy during their training, in part to set an example for Toshiro, which eventually would get to a point where Mizuki's arm would be cut off. Mizuki was too naive and able to see good in people even when there was nothing but harm. Shion was cruel but also caring. She actively hurt him, but he could tell she wanted him to improve and get stronger. This messy relationship kept Mizuki willingly chained down by the Hashimoto for years, as he believed he had no other way to evade his curse.

In the middle of the chaos, Winston was able to find a nearly finished, makeshift rocket in the base. After putting the finishing touches, he was able to launch the pod and escape to Earth. Little did he know that vessel was actually Hammond's, and he had worked on it for months hoping that they could escape together. Ingenious as always, Hammond was able to attach a spare capsule to Winston's vessel, and secretly hitched a ride when they blasted off. However, the cable broke when they entered the Atmosphere, and Hammond landed in a completely different spot than Winston, who had no idea his friend was following close.

Winston's ship would be intercepted by Overwatch agents in Gibraltar. After making landfall, the team was surprised to find he could address them in perfect English, as he required urgent medical assistance and lost consciousness soon after. After recovery, Overwatch made controversial headlines with the recruitment of their first fully non-human member. Winston proved himself highly intelligent, strong and agile, and when he requested to join the organization, he himself presented a case for personhood in court, following the precedents set by the Omnic Rights movement. Winston's reception was mixed at the start due to the ethically questionable nature of his mere existence, but he quickly proved to be an invaluable ally for the organization, as well as one of the most charismatic faces of the Strike team, becoming the face of the "Overwatch Adventures" cartoon, and by far the most marketable agent with a line of pluses and toys of his own.

Under the care of her grandmother, Kiriko would forge a close and lasting connection with the Fox Spirit, not just because of her Miko duties, but also through the Fox's anima that her father had created. Her grandma would often let Kiriko borrow the Anima ofuda as she taught her how to prepare her tools for Miko duties, and Kiriko quickly developed a strong sense of justice and empathy, using the anima's power to take on bullies and thugs, protecting those in need and healing them with her grandma's teachings.

Kiriko would spend most of her adolescent years as her grandma's assistant, while her parents, separated by the clan, worked together to find a way to take them down. For years, Toshiro was able to maintain communication with Asa exclusively through letters, in which he fed his wife intel about Hashimoto's plans. For years, Kanezaka would suffer through injustice and exploitation at the hands of the new reigning clan, and Kiriko was not blind to the city's pain. Not just as the shrine maiden and a follower of Kanezaka's local deity, but also as a close pupil of the Shimada's teachings. While the old clan was unmistakably corrupt and their activies were as bad as the Hashimoto's, Sojiro's stories and values left a deep mark on Kiriko, arguably more than they ever did on his own children. She would grow up to be a strong, caring leader, and a fitting protector for the city, as she vowed to one day take on the Hashimoto, rescue her father, and restore peace to the region.

Overwatch generally saw Winston as a possible fresh start, an outsider who had no preconceptions about Omnics, and with an idealized vision of human culture and history. He never saw the world for what it was, he dared to see what it could be. Since he lacked the assumptions of what was or not possible, he was the perfect mind to tackle the Oxton case. Alongside Wexler's team, Winston studied Lena's Chronal disassociation condition and began work on a device that he called the Chronal anchor. This harness was intended to pull Oxton back into the normal flow of time, and keep her from blipping out again. However, when tested, the device was only capable of keeping Lena anchored in space, not time. Her body was no longer reappearing in entirely different places, but it still vanished from the time flow uncontrollably. Still, progress was still progress.

During this testing, Winston realized that the matrix of the device was building up an unknown form of energy the longer Lena was kept anchored. Eventually, this buildup reaches a critical amount, causing Oxton's time fluctuations. After learning this, he scrapped the original design in favor of a new device called the Chronal Accelerator. This new iteration harnessed the mounting energy into a limited, controlled disassociation, essentially allowing Oxton to experience localized time travel at will. The device kept Lena anchored in time, and as energy built, she could use it to willingly blink or rewind back her own relationship with time and space, releasing the buildup without losing control. Oxton was stable and capable of living a somewhat normal life as long as she was in proximity to a Chronal Accelerator, but she realized that this gift of hers could be used to help Overwatch and the world. So, after being cleared from test runs, Lena began training to become part of the Strike team alongside Winston, who she grew to be close friends with. After all the time, he worked on a solution to her problem. Due to the trails of light left by the Chronal accelerator as she blinked through time, she would earn the call sign Tracer.

While Winston was intercepted by Overwatch and found a new home with the organization, Hammond's escape pod would take him to a far more hostile land. Crashing in the middle of the Australian Outback, Hammond used his ingenuity to survive the cruel wasteland. Scrapping debris and metal Omnics, he was able to modify the escape pod into a mobile unit for him to pilot around.

He would eventually make his way into Junkertown and learn about their culture, growing fascinated by the Scrapyard Arena and seeing it as an opportunity to prove himself. Using his knowledge of physics, and available weaponry, his mech became a rolling ball of death, which he used to climb up the ranks of the city. Going by the name of Wrecking Ball, Hammond became a celebrity among Junkers, though his identity remained secret as no one ever saw him outside the mech. Soon enough, Wrecking Ball went from contender, to uncontested champion, becoming a close ally and confidant to the Junker Queen herself, the first person to learn of his true identity. 

Hammond had found a happy, chaotic home among the Junkers and while he was still hurt by Winston abandoning him, he never really looked back now that he had his new life. On occasion, he would wonder out of the city to explore the wider world and acquire parts of his inventions, but of course, as the champion of the Scrapyard, he would always come back to defend his title.

One tragic night, the Oslo facility was rocket by multiple explosives. Cassidy was present but outside of the laboratory, as he had to attend a strategy meeting, so at the time Liao and Echo were alone inside of the building when the attack happened. The explosions knocked Cassidy away, but left him uninjured, as he rushed to the lab, he found Liao severely wounded, succubing to her injuries soon after, he sat with her while she died. 

Liao would be buried with full honors as the attack was being investigated, her funeral was attended by Mondatta himself, and many other Shambali. Following her death, many monks entered a voluntary full year of silence, as an act of mourning. Liao lived a life trying to make up for a series of events out of her control, in Mondatta's own words during his speech, "She sought the universal truth, she sought to repay a debt not her own, which had never been hers to pay, but which weighed on her thoughs until the end. We can only pray she is now at peace". Cassidy did not attend the funeral, as he had turned his attention to hunt her killers

In her absensce, Echo would be brought online in her unfinished state, to test her performance in field missions. While her AI continued to grow and evolve her capabilities and intelligence, Overwatch personnel feared that she could absorb the wrong input without adequate management, which limited her use within the organization.

Overwatch intelligence found out that Talon was behind the Oslo attack, and marked the beginning of a year-long war raged by Doomfist himself. The man envisioned a world of conflict, and Overwatch's peacekeeping activities quickly proved to be the greatest obstacle to his crusade. The man who ordered the attack was Antonio Bartalotti, a known arms dealer from Rome and member of Doomfist's council. Overwatch had been interfering with his smuggling operations, and he took the insult with a show of force as soon as he had the chance under Akande.

Reyes intercepted the report and gathered Blackwatch for an assembly. Gérard began to set up a new facility in the heart of Rome. From there he would be able to direct the action, disrupting Talon's hold on the area, and eventually pursuing his arrest. Antonio saw this as a threat and responded by attacking the Rome base as well. He had an infiltrator plant a bomb in the building, killing fourteen agents and injuring many more, including Lacroix. Reyes and Cassidy were present during the attack and aided in the evacuation, and both of them grew frustrated by Talon's audacity. Doctor D. Rosenberg attended to Gérard at the Swiss Headquarters, Reyes deciding to stay by his friend's side.

Morrison had charged Reyes with managing the fallout after Oslo, but Antonio was borderline untouchable, due to his high amounts of influence with the Italian government, and even attempting their usual tactics to take him down nearly got Gérard killed. Over the years, Gabriel had grown to despise the red tape surrounding Overwatch activity, and he had been able to work around them while keeping Morrison ignorant of his actions. As he prepared for his next move to counterattack, Reyes cared little about the consequences of his actions. He only had one thing in his mind; retribution.

Under his own authority, Reyes ordered a counterstrike of Blackwatch agents to infiltrate Antonio's palace by the Rialto, to apprehend him for questioning, despite lacking the proper clearances to do so. The team consisting of Cassidy, Genji, Moira and himself made their way through the Talon facility smoothly, until they found Bartalotti. 

Antonio taunted Gabriel during their brief exchange, claiming that he would be released regardless and this would amount to nothing. It's unclear if this was his intention from the beginning, but in response to the mocking, Reyes shot Bartalotti at point-blank, his body flying out of the window.

What followed was an all-out war in the city as Talon mobilized a massive force of troops to hunt out the strike team for the entire night. Blackwatch pilot, Carolyn Fio managed to evacuate the team but had been ordered not to identify the Italian forces. The drop-ship had not been cleared to enter Venice and displayed no markings. As the situation got tense, the Italian military gave them their final warning, and the team was forced to identify themselves as acting Overwatch agents.

The Venice Incident leads to the world discovering Blackwatch, and with it, all the skeletons Overwatch were hiding in their closet. The UN called for hearings and requested information about prior operations by this unknown division, but Reyes delivered clearly redacted and incomplete reports. Reyes argued Antonio's connections to the government meant he would have never seen justice if Reyes had followed protocol, but the damage had been done. Morrison was ordered to put operations on a tighter leash, and slowly Blackwatch would become gutted in everything but name,

This mission fractured Reyes' relationship with Morrison, and it would never recover, as Jack would often blame him to one degree or another for any trouble that followed. Cassidy too had become jaded by his mentor's actions and often wondered if he was really any better than a criminal. With Blackwatch getting scaled back, many agents were fired, due to being too much of a liability. Genji was allowed to stay, transferred into the Strike team for training before anyone could look at his background too closely, where he would begin to wear a mask to conceal his relationship with the Shimada.

Marzia had seen the death of her father. For years, they had clashed over how he managed the business, her believing that her input could help him make better decisions, but Antonio pushed her daughter away, wishing a different kind of life for her. Marzia was there when Doomfist came to discuss the plans following the Oslo and Rome bombings. She insisted on possible loose ends that could get them in trouble, but her opinion on the matter was disregarded by both her father and Akande.

The death of her father pained her, but she understood it as a grave he had dug himself. It was what came after that truly reshaped the course of her life. Marzia saw her father's business, as well as his seat on the Talon council, as her rightful inheritance, so it came as a cruel joke of fate when Doomfist seized all of Antonio's assets, and gave the council seat to Augusto Vialli, a Venetian who worked under Antonio, and was expected to take his place in the company.

Marzia was discarded without much thought, as Doomfist did not believe that anyone was owed a place at his table, it had to be earned. Thus, she was left with nothing, by the very same people who her father dedicated years of work for, the very same ones who ignored her insight, the ones whose actions got him killed. Abandoned and bitter, Marzia grew resentment towards Doomfist and his lackeys. She was not going to forget what they did, and if she had to climb her way back to the top in order to get her revenge, so be it.

Mauga's father was the leader of the Samoan branch of the Deepsea Raiders, and from an early age, his cell took Mauga many of their incursions, installing on him a heavy disrespect for the law and a feeling of doing something meaningful by defying those who sought to destroy the beauty of their oceans,


As their activities prolonged, the Polynesian Leagues began to send military troops to enforce order in their territorial waters, but the raiders did not hesitate to fight back. During a particularly intense battle against these troops, Mauga was critically wounded. He was half dead when they found him, and his heart in no condition for recovery, so the medics saw no choice but to implant a cybernetic heart, to assist his damaged systems. Mauga survived but was forever changed by this near-death experience. The first thing he did as he woke up from surgery was choke the doctor to death. He became a local legend when he returned to Samoa, known as the two-Heart Demon. Once back home, more upgrades and surgeries awaited him to keep up with his dying heart, which eventually gave out and was replaced with another cybernetic heart. 

The machines pumping blood to his body at double the power allowed his body to increase in size massively with his metabolism, but it also made maintaining his enhancements harder. Mauga lived at the verge of death every day of his life, at the mercy of either heart possibly malfunctioning. His condition taught him a valuable lesson that defined his way of life going onward: live every day carefree, because it could be his last, and while this attitude made him out to be a careless brute to many, in reality his lack of worries just made it easier to barge in and open doors to new plans.

While Genji and Cassidy were spared from the purge of Blackwatch personnel, Moira wasn't as lucky. Her reputation was a plague on Overwatch's brand, and most of the Scientific divisions had staff that had openly objected to her recruitment to begin with, before Reyes went behind their backs. Angela refused to absorb her into the medical staff, and so, Dr. O'Derain was dismissed, but it would soon become clear that her loyalty to Overwatch and their ideals would not last long, if she had any to begin with.

As the controversy surrounding Moira's involvement in Venice, as well as the applied capabilities of her research, it peeked the interest of some unconventional backers. Talon saw potential in Moira's research, and she gladly worked for them under the shadows, so long as they funded her experiments, which Talon wished to utilize for their own nefarious purposes. As she worked for Talon in secret, she maintained appearances in the scientific community, controversial as usual. 

Soon enough, she was invited to join a collective of scientists in the newly founded City of Oasis, a heavily advanced city where researchers could dedicate their minds to science restraints. Moira was installed as the head of the Ministry of Genetics, though her work is still unknown to the world at large. With Oasis's connections and resources, as well as Talon's funding and ways to get around the law, Moira has been freed from her shackles, and allowed to push the boundaries of her genetic research in pursuit of new breakthroughs.

The more time passed since the Crisis, the more the world moved away from the heavy militarization of the years prior. Volskaya industries began to face a heavy decline in Russia. The Crusaders, while still in use, were not actively seeing battle anymore. The Caribbean Coalition now focused on rebuilding and even then faced conflict with the governments of their nations, and most combat-oriented machinery and equipment ended up in the Roman Colosseo. With the ever present Overwatch taking the lead in global security and peacekeeping, most nations took a step back when it came to developing their own defensive technology.

The Inti Warriors of Peru made for an intriguing exception to this trend, as there were many factors that allowed them to remain strong. For one. Solar threading was already heavily used in all of Runasapi, making the idea of enhancing your own body to be compatible with it very appealing. The Intis could now serve as providers and healers for their community, and much like the rest of the Paqarina research group, they have become synonymous with Runasapi culture.

The unwavering presence of the Intis lead to continued enlisting of the locals, and over time one of the younger recruits began to stand out. Illari Quispe Ruiz had begun the demanding Inti training from an early age, and even back then her teachers saw immense potential in her, believing she could rise up to become the strongest warrior of her time. Illari took to this prodigy status proudly, dedicating most of her free time to extensive training and answering the desires of her community, so that one day she could finally live up to the legends she grew up around. Everyone in Runasapi was rooting for their young child of the sun, and as Illari grew older and stronger, it was clear she was meant to be the greatest of them all.

As the Turing Green project was progressing, it had grown to be quite controversial among the Omnic community. While most saw it as a true first step into integration, an opposition movement began to protest it as a token gesture, meant to absolve humanity from their actions by delivering the bare minimum. These tensions came to a boiling point when, all of a sudden, an army of Crisis-era war bots began to mobilize at Kings Row.

Null Sector claimed to be behind the attack, declaring London as a sovereign Omnic State. In their advance, the machines killed hundreds of humans, displaced several more and took several Omnics oposing the takeover as hostages, including Mondatta himself. People all over the world feared this attack could be the beggining of an all out war between Omnics and Humans. The British Government had no intention of letting Overwatch in after the mess they made in Italy, but Reyes secretly sent Cassidy to do Recon ahead of a potential strike team deployment.

27 days into the Uprising, Director Petras attempted to contact Morrison to no avail, as he was constantly put on hold. Jack suspected this was due to not wanting a repeat of a recent Cairo mission, where an Overwatch official was murdered. Petras most likely wanted to avoid the chaos of the humanitarian crisis, and the official investigation that ensued.

Prior to her death, Laio had been very vocal about the situation in London, and knowing she would have wanted to help, Morrison did everything he could to intervene. In spite of the British Government's reservations, he dispatched a small team consisting of the cleanest public-facing agents they had, Torbjörn, Reinhardt, Mercy and Tracer. Lindholm and Wilhelm had plenty of experience with the outdated war machines, and Oxton's unique abilities and familiarity as a local played a big role in the mission, allowing the team to rescue the hostages and repel the attack.

After years of scandals and arguably their lowest point in Venice, Overwatch as an organization was at the verge of collapse, but their success in London reminded the world why they were considered heroes to begin with. For a brief period, the tarnished reputation of Overwatch seemed like it could recover, and the organization lost no time in taking advantage of this, by commencing a propaganda campaign to clean the face of the organization with their most recent victory, with Lena herself being the primary subject of this publicity. The uprising was actually Oxton's first official mission, yet she quickly proved to be a darling with the media, becoming essentially the public face of the strike team. But not even Tracer's charisma could save Overwatch from the incoming storm.

Omnic support for null sector fell to an irrecoverable low after the uprising. The group had completely destroyed Turing Green during the attack and the project in which most Omnics placed their hopes for the future would never be picked up again. Perhaps most damning were the words of Mondatta, who labeled Null Sector as a terrorist group following his release.

Not only had Ramattra lost pretty much all of his supporters, but his closest allies, those who he considered friends, turned against him. Lanet warned him the war bots were too outdated and not ready for deployment, yet his impatience ended up costing her life. Nameless argued they should rally support from other Omnics instead of relying on a mindless, careless army, but Ramattra's insistence on keeping Omnics away from the conflict only ended up alienating potential supporters. It became clear to the last few members of Null Sector that the Omnics did not want their liberation, or even if they did, they completely destroyed any chance of it ever happening. 

For Ramattra, however, this loss only strengthened his resolve, as he proclaimed that they were going to free Omnics from this accepted submission, whether they wanted to or not. That any Omnics that opposed them were to be neutralized and held against their will until justice was served. In the heat of the argument, he told his friends that if they disagreed with his vision, they should leave. So they did. Null Sector went from a strong Omnic rights movement to a one-man crusade against the wishes of the very same people he claimed to represent, and in his solitude, Ramattra would only continue to spiral into radicalization.

When Gérard recovered from his injuries, he immediately turned his attention to investigating Talon's next movements. With Blackwatch on a leash, his resources were far more limited, but his Intel was able to stop several potential threats before things went wrong. Still, his gut told him Talon had some sort of mole on the is for given his familiarity with Blackwatch procedures, but he would not get to continue hunting ghosts for much longer.

LaCroix became a high priority target for Talon to take out and, after multiple failed attempts, they would resort to something far more personal. Former prima ballerina Amélie Lacroix, Gérard's wife, was kidnapped by Talon in the middle of the night, and while she was captive they subjected her to intensive neural reconditioning.

Gérard was horrified and focused all of his resources on finding his wife, while Morrison sent agents to guard the families of the rest of Blackwatch staff. In the end, Overwatch found Amélie months later, during a shockingly easy raid on a Talon base. Initial physical and psychological testing showed Amélie was unharmed and unchanged, but Gérard feared that something was off, given how easy the rescue had been. Two weeks later, his concern proved correct when Gérard was found dead in his own bedroom, killed in his sleep, and Amélie had gone missing once more. Overwatch never really rescued Amélie, they simply delivered a hunter to its prey. Lacroix's death was the final nail in the coffin for Blackwatch as a formal division, with Reyes choosing to continue his activities completely unreported, and Cassidy being sent out to do his bidding.

While official reports said Amelie had been taken by Talon. There was no real way of knowing what happened, they had no idea if she acted on her own, or if she was a victim. Amelie was hunted by both Overwatch and local police. However, that was not the biggest of her worries. She was haunted by the way killing her own husband made her feel. Amelie was often pretty apathetic and uninterested in many aspects of her life, but she still loved her husband, yet that moment when she killed him in cold blood was the most alive she had ever felt.

Unclear if it was due to the lingering effects of the conditioning she underwent or pure euphoria from a manic episode, Amelie was fighting the urge to kill again. With little options left and intoxicated by bloodlust, Amelie ended up turning to Talon, chasing the thrill of a kill again in spite of how much it terrified her. She requested to be given training to become a marksman, and consented to participate in trials for Moira's experimental program. The genetic treatment altered Amelie's physiology to turn her into the perfect killer. Slowing down her heart, which turned her skin a pale blue color, and dulled her ability to feel human emotion. These drugs allowed Amelie to kill without remorse, and strengthened the release she felt when going for a kill.

Under Talon, Amelie would go under the name of the Widowmaker, and quickly became one of their most effective assassins, turning every kill into a performance that captivated and devastated her audience, fully embracing her murderous cravings while suppressing the painful memories or her past with a heavy supply of drugs. She retreated to the abandoned Château her family owned, where spiders became her only company. And under the alias of Danielle Guillard, she was able to live a quiet Life I'm between missions, even visiting Gérard's grave on occasion, as the mixed feelings she got from his death were something Moira never managed to fully erase.

The conflict between the Deepsea Raiders and the Polynesian League had become a drawn-out stalemate, and once local enforcement proved insufficient, Morrison decided to intervene and dispatch multiple teams to aid against the terrorists. What was meant to be another unilateral victory for Overwatch by aiding local forces against a radical group like in London instead turned out to be an international scandal due to a sequence of failed missions during the campaign.

For one, the strike team had historically struggled in Maritime battles, which gave the Raiders an advantage amidst the chaos, but even on the land-based missions,  Overwatch struggled to keep up, with one strike near the Black Sands of Tahiti resulting in the loss of a pair of chain guns at the hands of the Raiders. The biggest scandal followed after an attack in Samoa. Search and Rescue was meant to evacuate the city where the Raiders were hiding, but Reyes pulled in his troops before the evacuation efforts were done. 14 civilians died because of his impatience, and had it not been for Freja and Emre, many more might have also perished.

The controversy got so bad that it ended with every country in the Polynesian League leaving the United Nations, as well as the full nationalization of Ecopoint: Samoa. Overwatch was locked out of the region and The Raiders remained active and now effectively uncontested. Their incompetence soured the view many of their best agents and scientists had of the organization, resulting in several resignations.

Reinhardt was well into his fifties by now, but his enthusiasm for battle was as young as always. Over the years, he had been offered promotions and out-of-combat positions, but he had always refused, choosing to stay as an active part of the strike team alongside the younger agents.

During a Global Security Summit in Asunción, Paraguay,a terrorist known as the Hivemind attacked, using unique drone technology to lock herself in with proprietary security data, using fifty high-profile hostages as leverage. Reinhardt was dispatched to command the rescue, and had been ordered to hold still while negotiations took place. The situation, however, escalated when Hivemind began to dispose of the hostages. Wilhelm realized that if he didn't act now, more lives would be lost, so he defied direct orders to save the remaining hostages.

In the end, 47 lives were saved, but Hivemind escaped with the data. While many saw his actions as heroic, many nations requested compensation for the stolen data, and Overwatch ended up in a massive scandal. To avoid further controversy. Morrison made the hard choice to force Reinhardt into retirement. Wildhelm was confused and cited his success in Asunción and King's Row as a reason why he should stay, but Vivian and Morrison continued to explain to argue that Overwatch could no longer act with the freedom they used to, and his disobedience had consequences. In the end, Reinhardt had no choice but to leave, and while he spent some time in Germany, he would soon move to Gothenburg to spend time with his God children.

This period of history was marked by an epidemic of social injustice across the world. From the list of Turning Green in Kings Row, to the resurgence of criminal groups like Deadlock, The Deepsea Raiders, Los Muertos, the Hashimoto and especially Talon, now that Overwatch has been kept on a tighter leash. Overwatch itself has endured a long streak of failures and controversies, making many people lose faith in not just them, but the establishment as a whole.

Under these circumstances, a counterculture movement began to rise in popularity across many places in the world: The Phreaks. Primarily formed by self-proclaimed anarchists and often equipped with illegal body modifications. They rose in popularity amongst protestors for Omnic rights, with many Omnics taking shelter with the group and seeking modifications, looking for a fresh start. While the movement was championed by many as the protector of the oppressed and downtrodden, many of the cells quickly grew radicalized and took their fight against the status quo to a more disruptive, violent level.

Marzia grew tired of being pushed aside and swore to prove her own worth, and one day reclaim what Talon took from her. Lucky for her, Rome was the right place for those looking to climb their way to the top, as the Colosseo opened the doors to fame and fortune to any daring enough to participate in the Gladiator games.

Marzia joined the ranks under the title of Vendetta, and while many underestimated her at first, she would conquer any challenge the Colosseo threw at her. She became known as the Wolf of Retribution for the tactic of choice, often letting her opponents have fun, thinking they had a chance, only to hit them twice as hard when she enacted her combat. While this play pretend gained her infamy and hatred, as she climbed up the ranks it would become the very same reason why many adored her. Her fame brought with it many powerful connections in the form of sponsors, some of them members of Talon's council themselves. And through her many wins she would come to acquire a formidable weapon, the Palatine Fang, a massive hardlight great sword, capable of cutting down anything in her path.

After years of service, Emre made the hard choice to leave the strike team behind. Far too many times, the higher ups ignored his pleas and advice, and it often led to tragedy like the many deaths in Samoa during the Polynesian campaign. He had grown tired of how lost protocol had gotten and the level of corruption leadership Reyes was playing in. Freja tried to convince him to stay, valuing him too much as a friend to let him go, but Emre already had his eyes set elsewhere. Many security firms had offered him positions, and he wished to try and continue making a difference outside Overwatch's structure.

Little is known of what truly happened to him, but his body was heavily modified by cybernetics, turned into a living weapon against his will by an unknown force. The God AI Chernobog, believed to have shut himself down in the crisis, was implanted into his body, forcing him to follow his orders or else endure as his own mind is overridden into submission. 

It's unknown what the true intentions for Chernobog's actions were, what caused his apparent shift of views towards humanity and what his relationship with those who did this to Emre is, or if the Program might have acted alone. Only one thing remains clear, he sees everything, and- HAVAINTO SYNTÄÄ HAVAINTOJA

Without Overwatch, Korea continued to deal with the occasional rise of a Gwishin attack entirely on their own. The ever evolving thread led Dr. Lim to create the Mobile Exo-Force of the Korean Army, a specialized unit for the testing of technology capable of keeping up with the Gwishin attacks and evolution. The program gave birth to a series of reconfigurable drones that could catch the Colossus by surprise, since, after all, what better way to fight off war bots than to innovate with your own.

For many years, these drones kept a perpetual stalemate against the Colossus, where they managed to defeat the Gwishin but never outright destroy them, but every few years a new wave of Gwishin would emerge, upgraded to counter the drones. MEKA was able to hold the Gwishin off for now, but the accelerating evolution of the Gwishin was quickly outpacing Lim's team, and following the near leveling of Busan during a particularly harsh encounter, it became clear that the team needed to explore alternative measures if they ever hoped to end the Gwishin for good.

Talon continued to taunt Overwatch for years, when they suddenly kidnapped a group of scientists, including a former researcher from Ecopoint: Osa. The mission to rescue the hostages was lead by none other than Morrison himself, with Ana as his back-up. They had decided to forgo the Search & Rescue team intentionally.

Talon shelled the entire area, awaiting Overwatch's arrival, and while the team managed to reach the hostages, it was with more losses than they could have hoped for. Agents Kimiko and seasoned Mirembe Atim helped with the hostages. All of a sudden, a Talon Sniper took down most of the rescue squad including agents Al-Farduk and Bayless, and Morrison was forced to order a retreat, but Amari refused, chasing the Sniper in a long-range duel. Ana would be taken by surprise upon landing a hit on the Sniper, realizing the person under the mask was Amélie Lacroix. The Widowmaker took advantage of the confusion and landed a shot that pierced through Ana's scope, and she never made it back to headquarters following the mission.

Officially, no one in Overwatch knew what happened and Talon's control of the area made it hard to search for her body. Ana was declared missing in action, and Sojourn took her place as third in command. For the longest time, Ana had served as a mediator between Reyes and Morrison. Without her, their already messy relationships deteriorated further. And publicly, Ana's failure made many believe that perhaps Wildhelm's retirement was long overdue, as the original agents appeared to be slowing down.

description.source:
Talon's influence grew across the world, as they continued to expand their network of control across the Caribbean. The Caribbean Coalition, who had long fought to stay alive against the wishes of local authorities, began to lose influence in the region as Overwatch intervention became less prominent.

Many ex-soldiers, like Baptiste, struggled to find work after their service was complete, and Talon took this as an opportunity to lure in personnel. Desperate for funds to help his community, Baptiste took on the offer. Early missions were easy, and they paid well, allowing Baptiste to get a taste of the good life and use the remaining money to support his local clinic.

It did not take long until the missions escalated, becoming more violent assassinations and resulting in many civilian casualties. Baptiste and the many other ex-Coalition mercenaries that took Talon's deal would go on to completely disrupt life on many of their own Islands, undoing years of the process they had achieved under the Coalition, all for a quick buck. It did not take long for Baptiste to begin feeling haunted by his actions, and question if he should even attempt to leave, but, of course, the only real way to leave Talon was in a coffin.

Over the years. The Deepsea Raider activities died down. With Overwatch out of the way, the world learned to fear Polynesian Waters and eventually their interventions began to become less common.

Mauga, however, was still thirsty for some fun, and the news of a New Doomfist taking over the gauntlet had just reached him. And it picked his interest. The mad man tracked down Akande, seeing him as a worthy opponent and challenged him to a no-rules, anything goes' fight, to which Akande agreed, sensing something was different about Mauga. After the long battle ended with a draw, both exhausted and unwilling to admit defeat, Doomfist was impressed by his ability and offered Mauga a place in Talon, where he could have regular upgrades and maintenance for his two hearts, and all the chaos in the world for his desires.

Mauga was placed in Captain Cuerva's unit, the same as Baptiste. The two became surprisingly close, with Baptiste being one of the few people able to see through his facades and calm him down. The Unit wrecked chaos across both the Pacific and the Caribbean, and with Mauga leading the charge, entire cities burned down for his entertainment.

In truth, Ana had survived her encounter with the Widowmaker, although it left her severely wounded and resulted in the loss of her cybernetic eye, which she chose never to repair. Ana was taken to a hospital under the care of Dr. Lee. Her injuries left her in a long coma, going by the generic Polish name of Janina Kowalska. When she woke up she did not remember who she was.

During her recovery, Ana wrestled with her years of service, and all the pain she caused as her memory began to come back. At her advanced age she began to resent the reputation she had earned, as one of the most efficient killers in the world. These haunted memories of an image of herself she no longer claimed and the wounded ego from her sniper duel lead her to request her doctor to retain her anonymity.

Ana now believed the world would be better believing she was dead, even her own daughter, as she feared Fareeha expected the fearless Captain Amari to return, not who Ana had become. And she remained a ghost for years, ensuring Overwatch never found her.

Sierra and Kendra survived for years hoping from one place to another, but one day right before her thirteenth birthday, Kendra would mysteriously vanish overnight. Sierra was left alone for the first time in her life, but her mother had prepared her for this situation. Following the emergency protocol, Sierra took a bus ticket from her mother's belongings and ended up back in Appalachia, where she met with her arranged father. James sadly was just as confused as Sierra for years, wondering where the two had gone. The only thing he knew was that government agents came to the house soon after Kendra left with Sierra, asking questions about a certain secret project: Naughton.

In spite of their loss, James and Sierra were able to reconnect as father and daughter. Under James's care, Sierra would grow a love for the outdoors and mountain climbing. With her father's support, she managed to have a relatively peaceful life through the rest of her teenage years, but she never gave up on the idea of finding her mom, and discovering what she was hiding from her family all these years.

With Ana gone, Sojourn stepped up as Captain of the Strike team, and with Lacroix gone and Reyes on a leash, she would also be placed in charge of pursuing both Talon and the new Doomfist. Her experience with cover-ops and counterterrorism back in Canada made her the ideal candidate to pursue action against Talon, without crossing the line and causing a stir like Reyes had.

Soon enough, Vivian's Intel came with a connection that would grant the team an upper hand against Doomfist. Maximilien, head of La Coterie, the man behind the booming Monte Carlo. Overwatch found out about his connections to Talon but had no legal way of proving it, and they knew that his lawyers and resources would do anything to get him out. However, they also knew that if they apprehended him, he would talk his way out with a deal.

Thus, a Strike team consisting of Tracer, Winston, Genji and Mercy was sent to Havana, where Max used a Don Rumbotico distillery as a money laundering front. The team managed to apprehend the Omnic after a drawn-out brawl with Talon troops right as a Hurricane was about to hit the coast, but as expected, it would not take long until he was released free of charge. Officially, there are no records of their interrogation, but behind the scenes, Vivian had won Overwatch their chance to take Doonfist by Surprise.

Following the Uprising, Ramattra traveled the world, learning of its history and philosophers, trying to answer a single question. How does one save those who don't wish to be saved? He pondered on this for the many years that followed, but could never reach a truly satisfying answer. In his research, however, he studied the Iris and its applications with his Nanite technology, and after a lot of testing, he realized he might have found a way to preserve his species. A way to liberate Omnics from the mortality of their Chassis, and finally, rejoice, from many as one.


The only issue was convincing the Omnic kind to join him. He had lost most of his supporters following the uprising, and while some small splinter cells remained across the world, they were not quite organized, and they did not even know who their leader was, a hermit hiding for years, who wished to keep Omnics away from active conflict. With so many Omnics outright rejecting the idea of revolution, and unwilling to put his supporters' lives on the line, Ramattra concluded that if it came down to forcing his own people into submission in order to save them, it would be worth it for the sake of their race.

In order to enact this rapture, he would need a larger army than what he used in Kings Row, and in order to build that he would need resources. Ramattra met with Doomfist in Cairo, seeking to establish a partnership, as his plans of Omnic liberation would seed chaos among humans all across the world, and he knew Talon would cooperate if it benefited their cause. Akande, ever the visionary, saw potential in the Omnic's cause. He believed it to be a noble goal, but doomed to fail without proper backing. With Talon's resources, Ramattra was able to begin the production of his warbots, and while Null Sector sat in silence, away from the public eye for years, under the shadows laid a massive Army comparable to Anubis' forces back in the Crisis.

Olivia had grown extremely confident in her hacking skills over the years as a member of Los Muertos, and she was one to challenge herself. She continued hacking through highly secured firewalls of many companies and organizations across the globe. It had become an addiction for her. But one day, while she was diving through the seas of data in her computer, she stumbled on the web of a global conspiracy. An unknown force awaited her at the end of her search, and it stared right back at her.

Olivia had encountered the first barrier she couldn't just break through. And with her identity compromised, she was forced to go into hiding, deleting all traces of her life never to be seen again.
That day Olivia Colomar had died, but not long after. Sombra was born. 

She had upgraded herself with cybernetics and stolen teleportation technology, not unlike the chronal anchor Winston developed years ago, and essentially became a living computer with one goal in mind: To find the truth about the conspiracy she uncovered, and figure out the true mastermind pulling the strings that collected the whole world. To do so however, she needed wider connections than what los Muertos could offer. She joined Talon in order to expand her own network of resources and to follow the clues left behind by this conspiracy, pointing to a certain rogue agent with the same Eye symbol carved into his chest.

Following the Intel gathered in Havana, Overwatch was now aware of Doomfist's next move. The man had made public apparitions before, following his predecessor's raids on Numbani, but this time he was set to make a short trip to Singapore, and every piece was placed to arrest him on the spot.

A small strike team consisting of Tracer, Winston and Genji was deployed to intercept the criminal, and while he was caught by surprise, he did not go down easily. The battle turned the city into a war zone and the gauntlet proved particularly tricky to deal with, as he dealt significant damage to Genji's cybernetics and caught Tracer off guard in the middle of frantic blinking, destroying her chronal accelerator and taking her out of the flow of time.

In the end, with both Agents incapacitated, it was down to an enraged Winston to go against the might of Doomfist, but in the end, the strength of the modified Gorilla proved stronger than the gauntlet. Doomfist was defeated and arrested on the spot. After years of terrorism and personal attacks against many veteran agents, Overwatch has finally won.

Akande was transported to Watchpoint: Grímsvötn, a maximum security prison designed to hold individuals with abilities and connections that would allow them to evade local authorities. A court-appointed surgeon removed his Gauntlet and once detached, it was sent to Grand Mesa for study. Years after the Crisis, it was still a marvel that left scientists dumbfounded as to how it actually worked, not made any easier by the series of safe locks set to self-destruct, making tinkering into its circuit essentially imposing without breaking it.

Overwatch higher ups came into question, in what developed as completely futile screaming matches against an unfazed quiet man. Reyes, in particular, was left alone to interrogate the inmate for an extended period of time, and while official reports do not disclose a lot of their encounter, behind the cameras, it appears as if Reyes was actually listening to what Akande argued.

Akande got through Reyes' skin, claiming he too saw how broken the global order had become. Years worth of red tape preventing Overwatch from catching him and many other criminals sooner, backlash against actions that needed to be done. He questioned the agent if he truly had made a difference in his extensive career, working for the police, the US Army or Overwatch, and if by locking him, was he really protecting humanity from a man in a cell, or merely protecting a jailed man from getting righteous retribution. Reyes did not answer his questions, looking genuinely disturbed by their implications. While his loyalty to Overwatch remained until the end, in reality, this was Akande planting the seeds of his latest and closest ally yet.

Overwatch's conflict with Talon did not just harm their internal staff, instead several civilian casualties resulted from their many encounters, and left several jaded towards the Organization. Findlay Docherty was one of the many victims from their all-out war. Having grown poor, with a widowed father that was very disconnected about his needs, Findlay was just a young teenager looking for some support from the system. His parents were Crisis veterans and regularly got checks for their service, and even if they barely allowed them to get by, it installed in the young man a deep respect for institutions. Tired of living in poverty and neglect, however, he sought a way out, enlisting in the military to help him pay for university, convinced that he would finally find success if he played along with the systems laid out in front of him.

Not long after enlisting, he was caught in the crossfire of an Overwatch in pursuit of a Talon jet. The Overwatch drop-ship had been hit, and it crashed into the flat Findlay grew up in, killing his father and leaving him trapped in the wreckage for almost two days. Findlay miraculously survived, but was left a triple amputee, preventing him from continuing his career in the military. The government offered him very basic prostheses and pain medication alongside a monthly check, but for Findlay he was still burnt by the injustice of it all. He lost everything he had worked for, and  the system gave him the bare minimum in return. Even Overwatch themselves could not bother helping beyond a speech by Strike Commander Morrison. That day marked a shift in Findlay's output for life, as he realized that he could not count on the establishment to have his back.

For years, Talon had survived under the shadows by focusing on the enrichment of the elite, and the benefit of the Council members. They really only sought money and power for the longest time, but it all changed when Akande took control. Akande's mandate of global conflict meant Talon was no longer sheltered in the darkness, and their actions needed to contribute to a cause, and while many members were indifferent to their organization's politics, naturally, there were those who preferred to lie low and profit in seclusion.

Following Akande's arrest, he managed to still have some level of control over Talon, bypassing his jailers' security and allowing him to communicate from the inside of his cell. However, the true person in charge of their everyday actions was now Augusto Vialli, Antonio's successor from Venice. Under Vialli's command, Talon would retreat into the shadows once more, for no cause other than what benefited the council table's pockets. His direction led to several assassinations and massive cuts in who got to have a say at the table, as the council struggled to earn bigger pieces of an increasingly smaller pie.

La Lupa herself was well aware of the direction Talon was being taken in, and she carefully watched as Vialli left them into ruin. She had earned the respect of many of her fellow gladiators, who were ready to answer to her any command. Using these connections, she deployed an attack on Talon's palace in Venice not long after Doomfist's arrest, thinking she would get an advantage by striking Talon at their weakest point. However, the assault was a failure, and it quickly became clear her numbers were still not large enough to take Talon head on. It would take years for her to be ready for another attack, but the Wolf waited patiently for her girl to strike.

Having arrested their biggest enemy so far gave Overwatch a new hope that public opinion would turn around for them at last, and that the streak of failures and controversies was finally over. But in the end, that hope died when an accident inside the Zurich HQ triggered an explosion that resulted in the destruction of the entire base.

Rumors and misinformation surrounded the press following the attack, with a particularly prominent one being the mention of Reyes and Morrison getting into a physical fight, possibly having caused the accident. In reality, both of the soldiers were caught by surprise in the middle of their fight. It had not been caused by anything they had encountered before, but rather an outside force with so little evidence left it would not be discovered until years later.

While many agents did their best to rescue survivors and avoid casualties, once the rubble set in, both Reyes and Morrison had gone missing. Morrison's funeral was a big event which his family agreed he would have hated, but they had little choice given his position. Reyes, on the other hand, had a quieter private event for his family and close friends only.

Jack and Gabe were not the only major profile names to disappear following the Zurich explosion. Genji had long struggled to accept his new body, and his role as a weapon under Blackwatch. The man was at war with himself and too often felt like he was not meant to be who he had become, so he took his chance after the Zurich attack and outright left without telling anyone.

Genji's journey of self-discovery would take him to many places over the years, but he would eventually reach the Nepalese mountains, where he crossed paths with the now Tekhartha Zenyatta, currently leader of the Shambali monks. Zenyatta would see Genji's struggle with accepting his new body and the man he had become, and decided to take him as a pupil, allowing him to deconstruct himself and achieve peace with himself once more. Genji would meditate with the Monks for years, with no one on the outside ever seeing Him again. He did, however, keep in contact with Angela, who he had grown to be extremely close. Even in the remote Himalayas, he found time to write her letters and keep in contact.

Calls of disbandment had happened for years since Blackwatch came to the public eye, but not with the HQ lost and the two highest ranking agents dead, it became clear there needed to be an intervention questioning the legality of ongoing Overwatch operations. The Petras Act hearings called upon all active members, as well as some retired ones like Reinhardt and closely related individuals like Sam English to testify about Overwatch, and while most agents generally sugar coated their experiences, Vivian Chase's testimony proved lethal for Overwatch's case. Vivian had grown to resent Overwatch's position later in its life, as individuals above her continued to disregard rules. In her own words, it only spread out the team thin, making them lose focus on their objective.

Many classified documents came to light during the hearings, and through that Reyes and LaCroix's vacations would be revealed to the world. With Jack presumed dead, he could not defend himself and was judged as if he had been fully aware of the illegal nature of their activities. Dr. Naughton also came in to testify that her boys would have been able to survive the explosion, which only made matters worse, as now many believe they went under hiding to avoid persecution. 

In the end, the United Nations passed the Petras Act, to be enforced by the International Justice Committee.  Named after the now former Directer of Overwatch, and IJC liaison William Petras, the act rendered all Overwatch activity illegal and stripped most Agents of their credentials and equipment Exceptions were made for cases like Tracer's, who required the use of her chronal accelerator.

A certain private security firm had begun to make a name for itself around the Middle East, and quickly began to expand its profile internationally over the years. Helix Securities International, backed by the Oasis Ministries, quickly became the go-to company for many different organizations. Thanks to the research and development of experimental weaponry and equipment like the flying Raptora armor, they were able to land enough of an Impression to be hired, contracted by the United Nations, as the guard dogs of the many Overwatch facilities that were not in the process of being decommissioned. This relationship led to many dismissing calling this paramilitary "Overwatch 2.0", in spite of critics pointing out how superficial of a difference that truly was.

In spite of that, Helix was able to fill the void left by Overwatch, at least when it came to peacekeeping and guarding important assets, perhaps exemplified best by their assignment on upkeep and defense of the Temple of Anubis in Cairo. Their legitimacy was also boosted by the addition of Fareeha Amari into the Raptora Unit on the Giza Plateau, having been hired fresh out of leaving the army now under the Call sign of "Pharah". Whether the mission is to safely guard the remains of the Naughton Vault at Grand Mesa or deal with escaped experimental Bat-Wolves at Oasis, Helix was always up to the task, bringing justice from above.

The Zurich explosion had not actually killed off Jack or Gabe, they both vanished after the fact, becoming living ghosts. But Reyes was left in a far worse state, when Talon found his body. Dr. O'Deorain concocted a series of chemicals just to keep him alive, further destabilizing his body's molecular phasing. Reyes was living in a never-ending torment, unable to go back to the world of the living, but all things considered, also unwilling to try.

Having been failed by Overwatch, he decided to give Akande's offer a try, working for Talon alongside another operative, Sombra, to retrieve an asset at a New Mexico site. During the mission, Reyes realized Talon truly lacked any sense of structure, goal or loyalty. Everyone involved was just doing so for their own benefit, loosely fulfilling a shared goal. After clearing off the way into the base, they discovered Subject: Sigma, peacefully floating in maximum security, only to find out an extraction team led by the Widowmaker was to take on the mission from there, as they were still seen as rookies.

This lack of formalities made Reyes wonder what Takin truly was, a means to an end, held together purely by a code of violence. A group of individuals collaborating purely due to twisted desires leading them to work outside the law, and the perfect kind of environment for Reyes to act as judge, jury and executioner, after so many years of red tape getting in the way. Thus, he took on the mantle of the Reaper, wearing a mask to hide his past and becoming a harbinger of death, taking matters into his own hands and forming an expansive target list of individuals he aimed at removing, with the very last names being his Talon coworkers themselves.

Under Talon's care, Sigma enjoyed more freedom than he had for several years. His fractured mind struggled to hold its pieces together, meaning he never truly understood the gravity of his situation working with terrorists, as he no longer saw himself as a prisoner. This, combined with the violent lashing out caused by the maddening melody he heard when his condition distabilized, made him both a complying hostage, and a highly dangerous weapon.

Talon understood Sigma as a human. Flawed, manipulable, and far more useful when willingly cooperating than when forced to. Taking advantage of his vulnerable state, they framed themselves as colleagues and patrons helping him further his research by providing him with everything he needed, when in reality they planned to weaponize both him and the fruits of his research Using their assets. Siebren was slowly able to gain control over his power, allowing gravity to abide by his will, moving closer to his life goal.

But in spite of that, his brittle mind was still unstable. Dr O'Deorain was in charge of supervising his condition and conducted several intrusive tests into his mind to study his condition. During this time, Sombra grew fond of the old man, taking pity on his circumstances and objecting to the way Moira and her scientists treated him. Sombra's kindness played a large role in Sigma's improving mental state, and Talon's continuous indulgence into his fantasies. And since Sombra lacked much loyalty to an organization, it meant now if they ever did something to harm him, they would have to deal with her.

Following Chernobog's command, Emre was compelled into joining Talon, where he would go on to become a highly efficient, ruthless killer, completely unlike himself. Many other Agents he worked with over the years noted he was pretty unreachable while working with them. Cold, quiet, and with a tendency to go dark in the middle of the mission, only to reappear right at the end to complete his objectives. Reyes himself got to see the man during his shared assignment in Luanda, and barely even recognized him.

From a raid on a R&D Facility in Burkhala with Moira. To an infiltration at a Guatemalan black site with Mauga, and a weapons facility attack in Hungary alongside Widowmaker, many agents took note of his off behavior, in spite of how selective he was about the missions he took. What's more, he would often outright vanish for prolonged periods of time, leaving no clue of where he went, only to suddenly come back when a particular assignment peaked his interest. What none of them knew was that it was not Emre making this choice and going against all his morals, but instead Chernobog, enacting his will through a husk of a man.

Over the years, Overwatch has fundamentally become a replacement for the old God Program system, building Watchpoints and Ecopoints to ensure global security and recovery. While the actions of the Strike Team and the paramilitary staff were more than questionable, in a lot of ways the scientists staffed at the many bases were some of the best humanity could offer, and yet they would go on to be blacklisted merely for their association with Overwatch. The Rouge God Programs Overwatch had monitored at Grímsvötn were relocated to the Atlantic Arcology under the care of the Martins, except Anubis, as the Temple was turned over to Helix Security, alongside many other bases.

Project: Echo had been deployed in a handful of missions after Dr. Liao's death, but Overwatch leadership was always reluctant to put it into full service. Without Liao's stewardship, it was deemed too dangerous to let Echo learn on her own, so she was shut down and placed into quarantine, lost alongside the many other experimental weapons and unfinished projects now guarded by Helix and other private security groups across the world. Liao's last dream, who had become a person of her own over the years, was essentially shelved like any other piece of machinery would have, unceremoniously buried alongside mountains of failed promises by Overwatch.

Ana has traveled a lot since going off the record, even passing through Junkertown once or twice, getting into brawls with the locals. When she ultimately settled on returning to her homeland, she did so with the intention of finally settling down, living peacefully and quietly. However, as more time passed, she noticed how much her home still struggled to recover.

Even decades later, Anubis' impact could be felt from its throne, as the Crisis left Egypt in ruin and too unstable to fully heal. Ana felt that Overwatch could have done more to help Cairo, and marked them as responsible for many of the problems plaguing the city. What's more, with them gone, Talon began to take over parts of the city and profit out of the chaos.

Ana could no longer stand on the sidelines after seeing her home succumb to endless tragedy. She took on the name of Shrike and became a ghostly vigilante, looking after her country from the shadows, taking base at a distant necropolis, where she took care of many relics and sent them over to a friend of the Wayfinder, Dr. Hamid Faisal. During her crusade, she would also keep a close eye on her family and close allies, writing many letters to Fareeha trying to explain her absence, but not once did she receive a response.

Years of competitive gaming shaped Hana's life when, just like her father, she decided to shape it into a career. Hana began playing Mecha Guardian V in high school, a massively popular online shooter with a strong E-sports presence in South Korea. Over the years, she quickly ascended through the rankings and became the number one player on the global scoreboard.

While still young, she joined the same team as an already established esports' player, Yuna Lee, a college student going by the username "D.mon". Even with many years of professional play, Hana, now going by the username of "D.va" to match her senior, constantly carried their matches with her aggressive play style, while Yuna anchored the team as their strategist. Together they formed a dynamic duo that consistently pushed each other to improve, in an unbreakable friendship.

The team would eventually go on the challenge at the world championships, winning on a landslide against their long-time rival Kyung-soo Han, "King". The two women had become celebrities across the gaming world, but Hana was usually in the spotlight, gathering a reputation for being a merciless opponent who played to win at any cost. D.va would become a household name among many Koreans and people from all over the world, both from her insane skills and actions per minute rate, as well as thanks to her blossoming streaming career, which kick-started her reputation. D.mon too, rose in popularity but was usually unaccustomed to the spotlight. While Hana showered in the glory of her wins, she would rather go back to assembling mecha figures in her dorms.

Without being able to rely on any system, Findlay was forced to find help outside the law to improve his condition. While researching ways to improve his prosthetics, he came across the Phreaks and their illegal body modding community, so he set out to look for the local cell in Scotland.

The group he found happened to be the home of one of the most prominent members, Touch up, who upgraded him with cutting-edge cybernetics that allowed him to regain mobility and manage the pain better. While he stayed with the Phreaks he got to meet many like-minded individuals, like Jackdaw, Boomslang and the Omnics Revel and Susannah, and over time he began to see them as a newly found family of his, even starting to date Susie.

Now as a fully fledged member, Findlay left his old life behind and adopted the new name of Hazard. Fully committed to the Phreaks' cause of tearing the system down and fighting the organization that perpetrated the broken status quo, he continued upgrading himself with further cybernetic augments, and began to travel around the world, quickly becoming one of the Phreaks' most prominent and radicalized members, Passionately helping other Phreaks and fellow rebels like the Deadlock gang, which commonly stole from large weapon empires like Arbalest and was willing to provide the Phreaks with firepower if they were able to met her price.

Overwatch's campaigns across America forced many gangs like Deadlock to scale back or lie low, but they never truly went away. And now that Overwatch was gone, it marked the start of a second new West. As gangs struggled in bloodshed and skirmishes to expand their territories once again. Ashe saw an opportunity to grow her influence through the chaos. Thanks to the negotiating tactics she learned from back in the day when she was still meant to take over the family business, she came up with a plan and gathered the heads of the major gangs with a proposal for them to work together, or at least not against each other.

Without having to worry about endless squabbles and with the shared assets of her former rivals, Ashe turned Deadlock from a notorious gang to a multi-state criminal syndicate. With their growth came many prominent new members, like the triplets, P. T, Terran, and Zeke, who quickly became some of Ashe's most notorious henchmen, as well as an Omnic Sniper going by Bars, who grew close both with Ashe and especially B.O.B., who had also undergone many upgrades to his systems to better suit his chassis to this renegade lifestyle. But perhaps the most eventful change in the Deadlock family would come from Frankie and Bez, who decided to get engaged around this period. As Deadlock grew, however, Ashe could still not let go of the missing founder. Even after so many years, Cassidy's betrayal pained her like an open wound, and even when she publicly trashed him, deep down she missed him enough to keep photos of them together on her holobike.

After many years of working in private equity to refine her craft, Vaira transitioned into the technology sector with her eyes on the price, the business from the family that once was ashamed of her. Be it through nepotism, bribery or sheer persistence, she made her way through Vishkar's board and became a key player in acquiring many deals outside of India. Even decades later, many countries were still in deplorable states from the scars of the Crisis, and Rio's dying favelas were seen as a prime venture for real estate.

When Vishkar architects Satya Vaswani and Sanjay Korpal were sent to negotiate, however, they were met with a more than skeptical government. Over the years, Vishkar cultivated a bulky reputation, with many of their projects resulting in rural communities and refugee centers paved over in favor of gleaming neighborhoods only the rich could afford. Back when Overwatch was still running, Reports from Watchpoint: Xining made it clear that wherever Vishkar went, displacement and class conflict followed. The government rejected Vishkar, hoping to collaborate with their rival, Calado's proposal instead, and as a result, Vaira resorted to more unsavory tactics.

Satya was one of the top architects among the recent graduates, and during her mandatory touring she quickly became a valuable negotiation asset. Under the moniker of Symmetra, she would start being sent on clandestine operations to uphold corporate interests behind the eyes of the law. In Rio, she was only meant to find some dirt on Calado, to use as leverage in the negotiations. However, by the time security forced Symmetra to make a run for it, she was unable to find anything on the competition. They were clean. Vishkar responded to this by blowing up Calado's offices, resulting in many casualties. While Sanjay assured her this was not part of the plan, and it was the price to secure the deal and build a better world, the incident was just one of many questionable moves that made Satya begin to lose faith in the company and their mission.

For years, the lives of the average junker were filled with chaos and misery, but they all generally fell in line with the commands of their Queen, as she knew how to keep order among the anarchy. There were those, however, that defied her and threatened the vague sense of stability in the city, and for someone to defy Odessa Stone, they would be either a genius, or unbelievably stupid.

Jamison Fawkes grew more or less his whole life as a junker under the car of the Demolitionist branch, a group that has made a living out of collecting metal and technology from the scraps of the Omnium and turning them into all sorts of explosives to be used by the other factions. Going by the name of Junkrat, he would grow a maniac obsession with chaos and destruction that quickly put him on the bad side of many of his fellow junkers, the Queen included, yet he was also meek and awkward, but really suited to the harsh eye for an eye life in the wasteland. His name would grow to infamy in the city after he began claiming he discovered an extremely valuable secret that lies deep within the Omnium and loudly claimed it as his, causing bounty hunters and gangsters to pursue him, many under orders from the Queen herself, to surrender the information on this treasure.

To keep himself alive, he made a deal with Mako Rutledge, an ex-ALF enforcer, who begrudgingly agreed to act as his bodyguard in exchange for a fifty percent cut of their earnings.
