Roadhog himself was a troublemaker, who defied the Queen almost since her crowning. He quit working under the Wreckers Branch for years, angering his old guilty members, and decided to set up shop literally on the outskirts of the Omnium gate, becoming an eyesore to the Queen purely out of disrespect. Mako hated the miserable life the ALF had brought upon themselves, but deep down he knew they deserved it. For all he cared for, as long as he had access to a hogdrogen gas supply to deal with the radiation, everyone else could rot. When he took in Junkrat, it was not clear if he pitied him, or if it was yet another middle finger towards the monarchy, but in his eyes, for as much of a nuisance as Junkrat was to everyone, himself included, they all deserved him, they deserved both of them.

Growing up in the depths of Siberia, Aleksandra Zaryanova lost her father in the crisis, and was left to take care of her sisters. Swearing to become stronger to protect her family and help her community rebuild, she began training her body, and quickly developed a passion for weightlifting.

As she grew older, she was identified by the national athletics program as a potential star, and taken into extensive body-building programs to represent the country as a professional athlete. Going simply by Zarya, she became known as the strongest woman alive, with a lifting record of 512kgs, shattering the highest Olympic score in her category. Zarya would go on to participate in many world tournaments, including the Olympic Summer Games in New York, where she won gold in spite of having a cold and a thorn trapezius. Having become an international star, the name of Zaryanova was proudly admired all across Russia, and her family's expenses were well taken care of by the fame of their big sister, the strongest woman in the world.

After his retirement, Reinhardt spent most of his days with the Lindholms, playing with the grandchildren and telling them tales of his heroic days. It was clear that he still yearned for a life of honor and glory. In the meantime, Torbjörn himself began a contract with the German army, where his years of experience in Overwatch maintaining Reinhardt's armor made him the best candidate to upgrade the new generation of Crusader Knights. Brigitte herself was now a fully-formed engineer who got to help her father on the Crusader blueprints during her formal apprenticeship at the Ironclad Guilt. Everyone expected Jeff to remain on this path like her father, when suddenly Reinhardt arrived with surprising news.

Tired of standing by on the sidelines, as evildoers reigned in chaos after the fall of Overwatch, he now vowed to go on a quest of chivalry, traveling across Europe in the name of justice like an errand knight of all, winning the hearts of the people by fighting for a better tomorrow. The Lindholms assisted Wilhelm on his mission by upgrading his old Crusader Armor, but he was even surprised when Brigitte requested to join him, acting as her squire and personal mechanic.

Brigitte had been very close to her godfather since she was a baby, and objected the most to Reinhardt's forced retirement, so in a way she saw helping him out as a way to make up for the failings of his old friends, and Reinhardt, overjoyed to have someone in his footsteps, gladly accepted to take her in as his pupil. Together the two traveled the continent in a small van for years, stopping at any town they could help them with their troubles and crushing any gangsters and thieves plaguing their lives.

The Rio deal's success proved Vaira's worth for many inside Vishkar's upper circle, which led to a promotion as Vice President of Operations and Development, but not everyone within the company knew the unbelievable levels of illegal activities she was getting up to behind their backs.

It was not just the more than questionable tactics used to eliminate the competition in Rio, as her many years accumulating wealth and working around the European Elite allowed her to pursue some personal projects and clandestine partnerships. Under the pseudonym of Domina, she had begun making deals with Talon, funding and profiting from their missions that destabilized towns and local governments by using them as potential scouting points for new business ventures.

While she was daring enough to collaborate with criminals, she was not a fool, and knew to keep her distance. Her seat on the council was always kept warm by Sanjay Korpal, a man who never fought for anything in his life beyond his next promotion. He would act as Domina's eyes on Talon and be the one to take the fall if their connections ever came to light. Under her advice, he would also engage in many other business deals, including active conversation with Guillermo Portero, the CEO of Lumérico in Mexico, looking for a partnership where the company could sell its energy to Vishkar's operations in Latin America. With this new underground network and a Vice President seat, Vaira went on to become one of Vishkar's most influential executives, on a mission to repair their reputation as the golden heroes rebuilding the world that they earned when the crisis ended, but behind the scenes she was willing to do anything to keep that mask up.

With Overwatch's disbandment, Winston was one of the most affected agents in the strike team. He was an idealist at heart who saw Overwatch for what could be, and not for the facts, and since he landed in their care, he didn't really have a home or life outside the organization. With the passing of the Petra's Act, Winston took the remains of Watchpoint: Gibraltar and made it his home, resting in seclusion when the world rejected his pleas.

Winston kept little contact with his fellow agents following the shutdown, as most of them went on to live their own lives. At most, he would quietly send Lena materials needed to maintain the Chronal Accelerator. In those cold years at Gibraltar, Winston often found himself staring at the moon and wondering what happened to his family at the colony, especially his old friend Hammond, who he never got to say goodbye to. But in spite of the silence, Winston wasn't completely alone. While the IJC decommissioned most of Overwatch's assets, he actually got to keep Athena alive. 

The program acted as Winston's closest friend and advisor, keeping good track of his diet as he had a tendency for ordering obscene amounts of peanut butter online, and perhaps more alarming, he was constantly keeping tabs on global news, seeing the world fall into chaos and coming extremely close to initiating a recall for all agents if it wasn't for Athena's interventions. So he begrudgingly waited at the Watchpoint, tinkering with new inventions until the day finally came when the world realized their mistake, when Overwatch was needed again.

Baptiste's time in Talon was awkward and short-lived. He made a few friends, sympathizing with Sombra on a couple of missions and getting really close to Mauga of all people, but with every mission that passed they began to turn more gruesome. While the first missions were mainly rescues and interventions, framed as if they were ending the reign of local criminals, soon enough things escalated into full-on violent coups, turf wars where Talon was seeking to takeover once they were done. Recent missions in Singapore and Makati led to many civilian casualties, and while Captain Cuerva said the operations are on level, deep down he knew that wasn't true. The turning point for Baptiste was during a mission while Overwatch was still active, when he saw a strike team deployed to tend to the wounded soon after they left. It made Baptiste realize Talon's goal was not to end the conflict, but instead seeding chaos and profiting from it.

Baptiste pondered leaving many times, but he knew that wasn't a true option. As Mauga put it, they were in too deep, and when he tried to leave he would be chased until he was killed. Things would take a turn in Monte Cristi, where the team was deployed to eliminate the leader of a local Playa cartel, Daniel Fernandez. When they breached the crime lord's safehouse, he was nowhere to be found, so Cuerva ordered them to tear the entire town down until they found him. In the middle of the fire, Baptiste came across a small girl, scared to death as he was destroying her home, now a soldier no better than the Warbots that burnt down his own town back in the Crisis. In horror at what he had become. Baptiste lowered his rifle and fled the scene, finding a fishing boat at the dock. Before he left, he was confronted by Mauga, who had been ordered to find and retrieve him. As Mauga stared at Baptiste, knowing his friend would not come back peacefully, he communicated to Cuerva that he could not find Baptiste. Mauga allowed Baptiste to go, simply saying, "call me when you're ready to come home." While Baptiste was thankful for his understanding, he knew sooner than later, Talon would come after him again, and he needed to be ready.

For three decades, the majority of the Omnium remained silent after Overwatch quarantined them at the end of the crisis. So it was a shock to the world when the Siberia Omnium, in the remote region of Krasnoyarsk, suddenly reactivated, and killing machines began to prowl Russia once more. Yet something was off about this particular instance. While the mass media was quick to call this the beginning of a Second Omnic Crisis, with Russia adopting the label for their propaganda, the rest of the world remained unaffected. It was entirely a localized problem.

The RDF ordered Volskaya to restart production on the Svyatogor, alongside new graviton technology for heavy defense. Katya Volskaya happily complied, as her company fell into irrelevancy for years and saw this as the perfect chance to get back to the top. One notable addition to the war effort was Aleksandra Zaryanova herself. The first attack in Novoanskoye happened the night before one of her tournaments, and as a local, fearing for her family's safety, she withdrew from the competition and immediately enlisted to defend her country. 

Zarya would quickly rise to become a Sergeant at the Novoanskoye Forward Base, and was personally given an experimental particle cannon, a weapon so heavy it could only be operated by Mechs, but for the strongest woman alive? It was lighter than a feather. Already a national icon from her Olympic career, Zarya's story moved the nation and gave many all over Russia the courage to enlist and defend their motherland together. In spite of this war effort, the Siberian Crisis would drag on for nearly a decade and result in the death of over 15000 lives, with no sign of stopping as the cause of the Omnium reactivating is still unknown.

Anubis, sealed in its tomb for over thirty years, had attempted to escape confinement before, but the multiple safe rails and supervisors that Overwatch's engineers provided prevented a full-on breach. With them gone, it did not take long for Anubis to crack Helix's firewalls and contaminate the sentry bots assigned to its throne. When the news of the security breach broke out, a Raptors Unit commanded by Captain Khali was ordered to neutralize the program. Helix encountered many problems that lead to many deaths and injured agents, alongside the disturbing discovery that Anubis figured out how to take over Awakened Omnics, as one of the troopers, Okoro, took his own life right as he sensed he was losing control of his own mind. While many of the soldiers wanted to bail, Pharah insisted there was too much at risk. Captain Khali conceded but noted they wouldn't get far without addressing the team's morale.

As the team made their way into the temple, fire fighting broke out between the security robots, killing Captain Khali. As per the chain of command, Pharah was in charge of pushing through the rest of the Mission. As they found Anubis, the program was finishing preparations to upload itself into the wider network, escaping confinement into the outside world. Pharah meant to destroy it but as a pillar threatened to crush her team mate Saleh, she decided to prioritize his life over the mission. Once safe, the engineer worked through Anubis' systems while Pharah wrestled with the sentries to buy him time. Together they managed to shut down the program and prevent another global crisis. As the team retreated to treat the wounded, Pharah had gained the respect of her teammates as their new captain, but most importantly, she reconsidered the meaning of her Udjat tattoo. She had the eye or Horus marked just like her mother, who used to say it meant protection. Fareeha now understood, it didn't mean she was protected, but that she was meant to be a protector.

The Exo Force Drones were able to hold back the Gwishin for a couple of years, but in due time, the Colossus adapted once more and began to disrupt the control networks. Without being able to control them remotely, the Korean Army was forced to come up with a new solution. The need to keep up with Gwishin adaptation led Dr. Lim to a similar solution to this familiar problem. Replacing the drones with reconfigurable mechs, inspired by Russia's resurgent Svyatogor technology. With these, a small task force of human pilots would be able to keep the war bots at bay with on-the fly improvisation and ever-changing equipment. Initial testing led to mixed results, with many dead and injured pilots. But when the team began to study the pilots that stood out from the rest, a common pattern became apparent, they were all avid video game players.

The controls of the Exo-Force mechs were not unlike those of most online shooters in the country, and their studies showed that professional players showed impressive reflexes and quick decision-making. The Korean Army decided to draft top talent from the Esports scene and similar fields with overlapping abilities. Mecha Guardian V champions Hana Song and Yuna Lee as well as their main rival, Kyung-soo Han. Seung-hwa Shi, a young analytical support specialist, and Jae-eun Kwon, a former F1 racer. 

Together, under the command of Captain Myung, they formed the current iteration of the MEKA squad, and finally granted Korea a consistent upper hand against the Gwishin. Their efficiency granted the team many liberties, and in concession to their professional backgrounds, they were allowed to customize the look of their uniforms and mechs to match their personal branding, using their professional name tags within battle and even allowing them to broadcast operations live from within the mech. While many of these broke military protocol, it allowed a massive boost in the program's popularity and opened the door to a massive propaganda machine, including several sponsors and movie deals for the different pilots.

Even the top agents of Overwatch were shoved under the rug after the Petra's Act. Tracer was one of the cleanest, most beloved agents the organization had ever seen, and yet upon returning home she went from the face of the strike team, to a dull desk job at the RAF, a position she later learned was meant to be an intentional demotion.

Unsatisfied with the quiet life and lack of heroism in spite of the resume and abilities, she quit the military and began a new life with her new girlfriend, Emily, at an apartment in Wilmington Road. While she was happy with her new life and partner, complementing each other greatly and spending their nights playing long tabletop campaigns, she was only mostly happy. In reality, she still felt aimless without Overwatch, missing those days when she was making a difference. It didn't take long before she found herself on the move, becoming a local vigilante, righting wrongs wherever she still could, stopping thieves and helping the locals in their daily chores whenever the opportunity presented itself. Emily herself supported her activities, seeing them as compensatory heroics, but deep down she only wished for her love to be truly happy once more.

During an excavation in Petra, Jordan, the Wayfinders found what appeared to be a small vein of an unidentified vanadium isotope, completely undecayed and in a condition not seen outside a laboratory. This was a rare enough find, but it's unique phase-shifting reactions made it extremely indestructible when solidified, and got in the way of the digging expedition.

The Oasis Ministries struck a deal with Dr. Faisal of the Wayfinders, to transfer the material to the University for further research. The head of the Ministry of Geology, Al-Shahrani was currently out studying seismic activity in the Red Sea, so the Vanadium instead found itself a temporary home in the Ministry of Genetics, at Dr. O'Deorain's request. Moira studied the vanadium ferrofluid for years, testing it's applications in medical trials and as an energy source, but this often put her at odds with the Ministry of Geology, which was set back way behind schedule by Moira's insistence to keep the cache.

Overwatch agents all over the world found themselves blacklisted from almost every single field. It did not matter how many years of service they had done or their accomplishments outside the organization, for most of them, just being associated with Overwatch was enough reason to turn down an application. This reality hit Freja particularly hard, as she dedicated her life to Overwatch, measuring herself by the increasingly difficult missions she had grown used to. Without being able to find a job again and after facing constant rejection, her self-worth disappeared overnight.

That was until a local police department posted about a set of criminals on the loose, which finally made Freja realize that she could still be of use in this new era, just not under search and rescue. Freja began to take bounties in the criminal underworld of Denmark, starting with small jobs to track down and capture criminals behind the back of the law.

Over time, however, this became a full-time compulsion as she began to take bigger, riskier jobs yet again. While at first she limited herself to rescues and taking down criminals, as the money flew in and the rejected applications kept rolling, morality soon became irrelevant, and she continued to chase down bigger fish. She took on the pseudonym of Gefn to protect herself from her feelings towards dubious clientele, and as her notoriety grew, so did her fee. It may not be honest work, but that mattered little anymore. The world turned their backs on Freja, so she carved a new path as one of the most efficient bounty hunters in the whole world.

Odessa was infamous in the Outback even before becoming the Junker Queen, with many legends telling of her journey to the Burninglands region, where she single-handedly destroyed all 5 of the metal demons, giant Omnic abominations formed into reassembled parts, that cursed anyone dating enough to wonder into their territory. While the veracity of these legends and the period they took place in are still not set in stone, one aspect of the story is indisputably true: the Queen's distaste for Omnics.

Having grown up as a waste lander, Odessa ran into many Feral Omnics over the years, and it shaped in her the idea of taking all you can in order to survive. Now as queen, her thirst for conquest was all the strongest, and having the means to expand her domain, she began to train Junkers from an early age to fight the many dangers of the Outback, including the Omnic Menace, as she called it. For years, Odessa, Meri and even Hammond would join the Scavenger caravans during their many raids into the wasteland with the goal of finding and exterminating any remaining Feral Omnics in the area, diminishing their numbers to near extinction, which only antagonized the few survivors even further. Still, this was not enough to satiate the Queen, who was now waiting to find the next target in her quest to rule the whole world. In the eyes of the Queen, the throne was where she said it was, and her kingdom started and ended wherever she felt like it, so while the Junkers are bound to the Outback right now, if the chance presented itself, they could begin to claim the rest of the world as their own.

Through many years of training, Ye Anran had become quite the name in competitive dancing and martial arts, but as she grew older, her studies encouraged her to make a choice between her disciplines. Living up to family expectations, Anran was accepted into Wuxing University's Fire College, and announced an early retirement from professional dancing to focus on her Wushu studies instead.

As a Fire College student, she quickly rose to become the star of her class. Wuxing's program trained the future military tacticians of China through the lenses of martial arts and ancient philosophy, so Anran's strict regimes and dedication sent her right to the top. This extraordinary competence, however, made her quite intimidating to most of her classmates, because while she was an undeniable role model, her harsh, blunt constructive criticism was tough to swallow for most, especially her little brother Wuyang, who was set to join her in Fire College only a couple of years later. Still, anyone brave enough to withstand the fire from her words, quickly found themselves improving alongside her, so even as a first year, Anran was the undeniable star student of Wuxing, making her parents proud.

Cassidy had fallen far from Overwatch following Petra's accords. Over the years since Venice, he has grown to question his role in Overwatch, if they ever did enough good to outweigh the bad, or if Reyes merely turned him into a weapon for his own crusade instead. He figured Deadlock would want nothing to do with him anyway after signing up to be a part of Overwatch, and for as much as he felt out of place with the good guys, he would not even consider Talon as an option. So, instead, much like Freja, he became a gun for hire, fighting causes he believed were just to get by.

He made many enemies during his many jobs and often landed in local jail cells, eventually losing his left arm, though the story behind this is still unknown. During those outlaw days, he would also meet Sombra at a bar down in Mexico and use her as a way to gather Intel on jobs, like many other lost souls tended to do when they spend long enough in the shadows. He didn't stay in the same place for long, often hopping from one train to another to move across the States. While resting on a ride on a Houston-bound Hyperloop, he saw a Talon squadron attempting to take over the train. The Gunslinger noticed the troopers were using Blackwatch tactics, not going after him but instead searching for something inside the train.

If he did not act he would have this whole ordeal pinned on him, so he began to take down the troopers inside the wagons, but the soldiers kept coming without any signs of stopping. As he made his way down the train, he found an ominous glowing box, seemingly Talon's target. Without concerning much about the nature of the payload, he tossed it out of the wagon, confident that if Talon got to keep it they would leave the train and its civilians alone. Cassidy got to enjoy the rest of the ride as a proper lawful passenger, and when news broke out that the attack was being blamed on him, the staff kindly agreed to tell the truth to the police and fudge the arrival times enough to allow him to make an exit.

After fleeing Talon, Baptiste sat in Tortuga for a while, but it didn't take long before Talon began sending agents after him. One after the other they would try to silence him, many of them Baptiste's old comrades. He knew too much and was too dangerous to be let go, and Cuerva himself wished they could still talk some sense into him, but if they failed to capture him, they would be forced to eliminate him.

During their attempts, however, several of the operatives in Cuerva's units went missing, and a letter made its way back to Cuerva containing their emblems torn straight out of their uniforms. Contact with Cuerva himself was lost not long after, but he always said that Baptiste had the devil's own luck on his side. His team made the mistake of going after Baptiste one by one, allowing him to take them down and leave Cuerva for last.

Knowing Talon would not stop, Baptiste began to drift from place to place, never staying too long, only occasionally returning home to check on his local clinic. He wished to help make a better world in any way he could, to make up for his mistakes. For some people, this meant a band aid, for others, a bullet. He knew he couldn't erase the past, but he could at least make a difference where it mattered, so he began carrying out humanitarian efforts while keeping a low profile on his travels, trying to make a difference while still on the run.

Junkrat and Roadhog continued wrecking havoc in Junkertown, angering most of the city. After a string of incidents that placed them on the Queen's bad side, enough was enough. Odessa's hands to put some order if she wanted to still be respected amongst the Junkers.

As an act of mercy, the Queen did not order their execution, instead removing them from the city and threatening to properly kill them if they ever tried to return. Junkrat blamed the situation on Roadhog without much thought, and quickly began to hatch a plan to break into the city and enact their revenge.

There are two things that solve any problem, according to Junkrat himself: money and explosives. In order to set his secret master plan in motion, the pair needed a lot of riches, so after wandering their way out of the outback, they began an international crime spree. Reported by A Moment in Crime's programming, the Junker duo gained notoriety for a string of robberies, including other crimes like arson, murder, and even stealing the crown jewels in London. Going by the creed of "No job too big, no score too small", they spread mayhem across the whole world, causing a loss of millions in property damage and injured casualties, eventually earning a bounty of up to $25 million.

For years, Sierra kept looking for her mom, trying to find more data on the only clue that she had, Project Naughton, but any information about it was highly classified, now transferred to what was left of Watchpoint: Gran Mesa to be guarded by Helix Securities. After graduating from high school, she applied to join Helix, seeking to gain the security clearance needed to review the Naughton Vault.

Her unique physical skill and exceptional intelligence quickly allowed her to soar within the organization, where she was assigned to lead the Perilous Operations Team, colloquially known as Helix's Summit Squad, a division specialized for missions that took place in harsh terrain. Equipped with a plasma rifle and a remote-operated traversal helper drone, R.O.T.H, which she personally nicknamed Dorothy, Sierra went on to spearhead rescues in narrow ridges and stop criminal operations in cave systems. From Gran Canyon to Niagara Falls, she conquered every challenge and quickly gained notoriety amongst Helix's American staff as one of their most invaluable assets.

When Vishkar took control of Rio's renovation, the locks were told they were going to make Rio a better place, but it went down the same way all their other projects did. Failed promises, displacement and poverty, enforcing of curfews and ordinances to suppress local traditions, and even exploiting the populace for cheap labor. But there was still one silver lining for the people of Brasil in the form of Benicio Dos Santos.

Benicio was a local scientist who dedicated his life to the study of sound and its applications as a medium for healing technology. He had joined Vishkar so that, with their help, he would be able to fully develop his prototypes into something that could help his people. Instead, when he presented his inventions to Vishkar, they claimed ownership of the technology and adopted its more destructive capabilities into police equipment, to be used against protesters for quick and forceful neutralizing of anyone who got in their way. 

This technology was used even outside of Rio, later adopted by the London Police to suppress the Omnics of the Underworld, with Vishkar's own vice president Vaira Singhania adopting the technology into her assistive arms for personal protection. What was meant to be Benicio's gift to Rio was turned into yet another tool for oppression, and while Vishkar thought this was just like any of their previous projects, this time the water was beginning to boil, and the people of Rio were beginning to grow tired of their games.

With Overwatch gone, Angela lost her limitless funding and immense staff of the best doctors in the world, the time for long miracle-working campaigns across the world was over. In spite of this, however, Angela's dedication to helping those in need never died. She distanced herself from Overwatch and instead dedicated herself to supporting smaller scale medical operations across the world, traveling to war and crime-ridden areas to take care of those affected by all sorts of tragedies.

She traveled from Poland to South Korea aiding those affected by Talon and the Gwishin, eventually finding herself in Venezuela, where she crossed paths with Baptiste, another wandering medic seeking to heal the world. Everywhere she went she felt the echoes of Overwatch and the guilt of all the problems it left behind after falling apart. Her charity eventually took her to Egypt, where, in spite of masked vigilantes and the efforts of Helix's, Talon's shadow still haunted the streets of Cairo. 

She settled near Pharah's place and the two of them shared a lot of their free time together, connecting after Overwatch. Finally, Fareeha developed a bit of a crush on Angela, though she never knew if the feelings were mutual. For two years she spent her days taking care of those affected by the skirmishes, and while many of the locals shut her down, telling her Overwatch had done enough damage already, she did not become a doctor to be thanked, so she stayed to help anyone she found in need. She even considered applying to join a proper hospital, but even for the great Angela Ziegler, guardian angel of the world, a career with Overwatch in her CV wasn't exactly what most professionals were looking for at the time.

Reinhardt's chivalry quest took him to many places in Europe. From protecting Omnics against violent aggressors to finding thieves and retrieving their stolen goods. Together, he and Brigitte built a reputation for their acts of charity, and the spontaneous nature of their interventions allowed them to bypass a lot of the restrictions imposed by the Petras Accords, letting them help those in need without raising an eyebrow.

While stopping for fuel and supplies in a remote Romanian town, the knight and his squire found a ghost town, where the citizens were terrorized by the Dragons, a gang of bikers who raided villages they marked as part of their territory. The local authorities did not have the resources or experience to deal with such a spread out problem, so when the duo found the gangsters, Reinhardt immediately took action and attempted to put them in their place. The Dragons, however, took a child hostage, forcing Reinhardt to endure a beating in the streets as they mocked him for being stuck in the past.

Anyone else would have turned away and let the issue be handled by the government, but Reinhardt, in spite of his old weakened body, could not stand by it. Brigitte located the Dragons hiding out at a nearby abandoned factory, and after fixing up his armor, dropped Reinhardt off to fight the Dragons. Fully embracing the poetry of their tale, he envisioned his foes as mighty reptiles coming against a knight of old, and thanks to his trusty Crusader Armor, he was able to take all of them at once and beat them into swearing to never return. Once they were thanked by the locals, and made sure the gangsters kept their word, the duo took off, wondering where their journey would take them next.

While Torbjörn was officially retired after the Petra's Act, he still felt there was a job to be done, and unfinished business to clean up. He had spent most of his life creating weapons, many of which were used by Anubis to kill millions. To this day, the weight of his involvement troubled Lindholm, and while many of his creations were either destroyed, or at the very least in good hands, there were still plenty of them that had been stolen or stashed away. Afraid that his technology could fall into the wrong hands, he paid close attention to the news to track down potential misuse all by himself. One of the more extreme cases Lindholm found himself in was in the young nation of Kurjikstan, where out of nowhere a Titan Unit resurged and attacked the capital of Boklovo. 

The full might of the military was deployed to stop the war machine but nothing they used could get behind its defenses, but as the Colossus headed downtown, Torbjörn had managed to infiltrate it from the ground. Having played a part in the creation of the Titans, Lindholm was well familiar with its blind spots and how to get past its defenses. As he made his way to the pilot cabin, the man behind the attack made himself known as one of Lindholm's old colleagues. Sven, a fellow Ironclad from the old days, is controversial for his way to cheat through engineering shortcomings. 

As he tried to reason his madness with Torbjörn, he explained how Kurjikstan, a known dictatorship bent on expansion, was an unpredictable danger on the global scale. He had stolen the Titan to use it to preserve global balance, and Boklovo was meant to be a demonstration of the ultimate weapon, and what it was capable of under a responsible government.Torbjörn however, saw Sven as nothing but a profiteer, awaiting to give his creation to the first "Responsible Government" willing to pay the price. Torbjörn was able to neutralize the enraged Sven as he charged at him, and while the Titan unit was shut down, most of Boklovo had already been left in ruins.

Brigitte's duties as a Squire were many, from providing upkeep to the Crusader Armor, to taking care of Reinhardt himself, whose body was struggling to keep up after years of combat. His overenthusiasm for the Dragons put him and others in danger, and while bandaging him up and minimal repairs to his armor helped him get back up and win the battle, it was clear to Brigitte that being Reinhardt's mechanic wasn't enough.

The best way to provide support and relief for the old man was to join him in battle. Over time, Brigitte collected scrap to design a lightweight take on the Crusader suit, determined to become a warrior in her own right. Reinhardt helped out too, training her in combat so that when the time came, she was ready to fight at his side. Together, the duo joined shields to protect the innocent and right the wrongs of the world, and Brigitte, no longer on the sidelines, became an inspiration for everyone who crossed their path.

Benicio's son, Lúcio Correia Dos Santos, was a loud voice in Rio's community. For years, he worked alongside like-minded people to help improve the living conditions of those affected by the Crisis, making sure that the children in the favelas had healthy meals and library books, but to adults, he was more well known for the underground concerts he hosted as a DJ, believing that music would bring people together and help lift their spirits.

Lúcio was naturally his father's strongest supporter, and when Vishkar stole his tech to use against his people, he was the one shouting the loudest against their corruption. Tired of Vishkar's oppression and wanting to vindicate his father, Lúcio would break into Vishkar's facility to steal the Sonic technology. Using their Hardlight generators, Lúcio would create equipment that would even ground against Vishkar's enforcers. A pair of light-bladed skates capable of grinding on walls, a handheld sonic blaster and Audio amplifiers capable of outputting the therapeutic sound waves from his father's research. Using these new tools, Lúcio took to the streets to rally the masses against Vishkar, starting a revolution that quickly overwhelmed the architects and enforcers, leaving them with no choice but to temporarily leave the city. Lúcio's leadership made international headlines and helped bring attention to the dire reality of Vishkar's actions, causing a major blow for the company that made many nations, especially in Latin America, unwilling to go through with any more projects.

Overnight, Lúcio had become a global celebrity, with his music reaching the top of the charts. In a matter of weeks, he went from local performances, to filling up entire arenas and starting a world tour: Synaesthesia Auditiva. With his newfound fame, Lúcio realized that he had the attention of the entire world, and with it a chance to be heard, and change the world for the better. Alongside his touring, he would become a very vocal activist, particularly against large corporations like Vishkar and the injustices that people lived under their management. His father, of course, had become one of his strongest supporters as well, happy to see that his son had become a national hero, like those Overwatch agents he always grew up wanting to be, and that while many framed him as a criminal, a rioter and a thief, in his hands, his technology had found a way to help the world, and make the plies of his people heard.

Five years after Overwatch shut down, a series of attacks on different financial institutions, including Germany's largest bank, large shady corporation like Lumérico, and particularly, former Overwatch facilities, all sparked global attention due to being carried out by a single nameless man with a number 76 marked on his back. The latest of these assaults took place at Watchpoint: Gran Mesa, where the masked man stole a pulse rifle and evaded Helix troops. 

None of the personnel was killed, but one of the injured soldiers mentioned the intruder had strength beyond what any human could achieve, and likely came from a military background. Following the Grand Mesa breach, the United States began an international manhunt for the culprit, and with the release of declassified documents from the Zurich Archives, many were quick to point out that Jack Morrison's designation under the SEP was Soldier: 76.

The many conspiracy theories that had formed around Morrison's death turned out to be true; he had survived the Zurich explosion, much like Reyes. Jack had spent years building Overwatch into his legacy, his entire life was defined by the organization, so now that it was gone, all he had left was a one-man war, to find those responsible for the fall of Overwatch. Now fully healed from the wounds of the bombing and armed with cutting-edge technology, he was ready to chase the ghosts of Overwatch's pasts for as long as it took to find the truth behind this conspiracy.

While the MEKA squad was able to take Gwishin head on in most encounters, the ever-evolving machines often found ways to overwhelm the young pilots. During one particular attack during a thunderstorm, the team was barely able to stop the Colossus, leaving their mechs out of commission and the pilots heavily injured, except for D.va, who managed to end the attack relatively unscathed. While the media reported that D.va was celebrating her victory as the rest of the team took leave, in reality Hana had remained at the base assisting Dae-Hyun with mech repairs. The weight of Korea's safety had begun to take a mental toll on Hana, and she spent most of her time preparing for the next attack, which was just around the corner.

Usually, the Gwishin spread out their incursions for several months, but this time a fleet of five drones had emerged in the middle of the night, merely a week after the last attack. With the rest of the team still recovering and their mechs under repair, it was up to D.va to handle the situation on her own. The Gwishin drones overwhelmed Hana, as she was able to take down two of them, but the rest evaded her fire and continued their route to the city. As D.va pursued them, she managed to take down two more, but her mech was too damaged to take on the last one.

While asking Dae-Hyun for help, they noticed the mech's reactor was becoming unstable. Hana suggested an overload, using the explosion to blow up the last Gwishin, and while Dae-Hyun was opposed to such drastic action, the dire circumstances left them no choice. The mech was set to self-destruct in sixty seconds, but fearing the Gwishin would launch its attack before that, Hana chose to pin down the warbot as she ejected herself from her mech, aiming at the core with her light pistol to trigger the explosion early. Hana's unconscious body fell into the sea, before a search and rescue party was able to recover her. She had saved Busan once again and while the media reported she had emerged without a scratch, in reality she had broken a leg and an arm, placing her out of commission with the rest of the squad while she healed, but still choosing to stay at Base to help Dae-Hyun with repairs.

In the middle of the black forest rested the remains of several Bastion units, defeated by the Crusaders and the German Army during the Crisis, slowly but surely reclaimed by nature, undisturbed for years. One day a miracle happened, a severely damaged unit suddenly reactivated, now overgrown with vines and roots, covered in rust and nested upon by many small animals including a particularly curious yellow cardinal.

The Bastion unit appeared to be conscious, like any Omnic awakened by the Crisis. Dr. Liao had long thought Bastions lacked the hardware requirements for sentience, which makes the nature of this Omnic's personhood still a mystery. The Awakened Bastion was filled with wonder about the beauty of the forest that surrounded him, and set out to discover its surroundings, growing attached to nature, and the cardinal that had been imprinted onto his chassis.

In spite of his gentle, even harmless demeanor, the Bastion unit was still dangerous. While Anubis' programming was nearly lost, the core combat capabilities of the machine were still functional and occasionally took over when Bastion sensed a threat. Not only that, but Bastion had scanned other units while scouting the forest, finding out his passage as a warbot and his final directive before being shut down to attack a nearby city. Luckily, Bastion's autonomy and his love for life and the wilderness distracted him from following this directive, choosing instead to remain with his animal companion, but as time passed, humans would begin to encounter the wondering Omnic, attacking him out of fear from the horrors of the Crisis. This led Bastion to largely avoid wandering in populated areas, remaining hidden in the European wilderness.

The more Tracer dealt with local crimes in London, the more she became aware of the daily injustices of the Omnic Population. While she played a role in stopping the Null Sector Uprising years ago and wasn't hostile towards Omnics, the harsh reality of her home country did not exactly settle in until she took a look on the streets for herself. With Turing Green abandoned, the Omnics had no choice but to settle with their already deteriorating Underworld, and the Sonic weaponry that Vishkar had given to the police only continued to enforce curfews on their activity. It is not surprising then that many had to resort to stealing from the outside world in order to survive.

While on her daily patrols, Tracer saw the police pursuing an Omnic gang. After cornering one of the thieves, the Omnico, going by Iggy, explained that the modulator she stole was needed to maintain the Underworld grid, and that no matter what she tried, humans refused to sell it legitimately. Tracer listened to Iggy and attempted to de-escalate, pointing out their shared love for punk music and getting Iggy to show her around the underworld to see her vintage Vinyl collection.

While this interaction allowed Tracer to bond with the Omnics, it also opened her eyes to the deplorable state in which the neighboring Omnics lived, and while Iggy's friends were welcoming her, many other Omnics, including their gang leader, Kace, were actively antagonistic and scolded Iggy for bringing a human to their home. Following her visit to the Underworld, Lena began to search for parts that could help maintain the Underworld grid, using her own money to acquire parts that Omnics couldn't get and even getting in contact with Winston for advice for repairs. Even if not everyone was welcoming of her help, she still wished to make the lives of Omnics in London easier, especially now that she had made some friends within their community.

Following the assault on Gran Mesa, reports placed Soldier: 76 near Dorado, targeting Lumérico power plants after having crossed the border. While Los Muertos had seen a rise in popularity over the years, many of their members were still gangsters, denying the law, endangering civilians and stealing from anyone they could, even little girls. Just because their cause came from political uproar did not mean they were not thugs, and this placed them as Soldier: 76's next target in the area.

The man pursued a truck of Los Muertos members, leaving a clear message by beating one of them with a charred Piñata. When the criminals attempted to flee, they struggled to keep up against the relentless man and his impeccable aim thanks to his visor. As a last resort, one of the thieves lobbed a grenade at a little girl that had found herself caught in the fighting during her trip to the store. Morrison's instincts kicked in, jumping to protect the girl from the explosion, while the gangsters managed to flee the scene.

As he recovered from the attack, the little girl recognized the man as one of the Heroes of Old, from the Overwatch posters. Jack disagreed, stating that was not who he was anymore. He vanished in a split second, but secretly watched from the Rooftops as the girl made her way back home safely. The reports fueled the fire of speculation and conspiracy over the man's identity and, while the reward money for his arrest continued to go up, many who crossed his path came to the same conclusion as the little girl. The man was a hero, even if he denied it.

Around this period, an Orange Cat who would go on to be known as Fika was born. While little is known about her origins, it's clear from her behavior that she is a lot smarter than any normal cat, and her distaste for Lucheng Interstellar could possibly link her to their nebulous project Star Companion, a similar experimental program to the Genetic Therapy used in the Horizon Lunar Colony.

Over the years, Kiriko's grandmother would begin to feel the weight of her years, and eventually passed away, leaving Kiriko as the primary caretaker of the Tetsuzan Shrine of Kanezaka, moving into a new apartment by herself at the request of her mother, who forbade her from continuing their Miko duties, instead wishing for Kiriko to join her again. Their relationship had been strained over the years, with Kiriko finding herself at a crossroads of two paths, that of a spiritual healer like her grandma and a deadly blade like her mother. Kiriko's attachment to her faith caused the two to fight and not talk to each other in weeks, not helped by Kiriko's poor diet choices and the fact that Asa did not know she now had the Fox Anima made by her father.

During the Fox Festival, Kiriko found her mother in yet another discussion with her mother, when suddenly she heard a commotion outside. The Hashimoto were bothering Mr Yoshida,a worker at Kiriko's apartment who was coming back from the festival with his granddaughter. As the Hashimoto threatened the helpless man with the money his son owed to the clan, Kiriko had already vanished from her room, reappearing in the hallway and taking on a full gang of Hashimoto all by herself, while trying to keep the old man and the child safe and healing their wounds with the Anima Ofuda. The night of the Fox Anima was enough to reinvigorate anyone in its field, looking almost like possession and scaring the Hashimoto thugs away.

Asa had noticed her daughter's absence and observed the encounter from the door, realizing she had her grandma's kindness, but the fighting spirit of her parents, and most importantly that all the times she brought up the Fox Spirit, it wasn't just blind faith, but the last gift from her Father acting as a guardian companion. When Kiriko returned, the two had heart-to-heart and Kiriko finally agreed to move back with her mom, even if just briefly. Together, the pair swore to keep Kanezaka safe, using the Fox Spirit as a symbol of protection against the Hashimoto. While Toshiro was still a hostage, he was at least allowed to send occasional letters back home, even including a small dagger forged as a gift for Kiriko, and a symbol of the unbreakable spirit of their family, as the last resistance of Tokyo, and the blade that protects the innocent.

While Sombra operated for Talon, she kept her own agenda with Los Muertos, and continued to aid in their efforts against the Mexican Government and Lumérico. With the help of a couple of clowns, Junkrat and Roadhog, who were breaking their way into the local bank, Sombra took advantage of their distraction to bypass Lumérico Security, where she found all of Guillermo Portero's dirty laundry. Days before the inauguration of the company's latest power plant in the town of Dorado, Lumérico's website was hacked, alongside Portero's own email, both accusing him of corruption and promising a full disclosure. 

Soon after, documents were released indicating that Portero used the company's funds as his own piggy bank, inappropriate correspondence with several female officers in important positions in exchange for favors, and personally brined officials to create a system of paybacks that continued benefitting Lumérico. The files laid out a plan to seize land through government expropriation to continue expanding their facilities, as well as emails of conversations with Vishkar's employees like Sanjay Korpal, in regard to exporting their energy systems to the company, not long after the riots in Rio soured the company's reputation in Latin America.

The hacks reached international attention from Atlas News, while Mexican authorities pursued the culprit, but they had bigger issues to handle now that the public knew the truth about their War Hero Politician. Sombra's efforts incited a popular revolution against Lumérico, and a rise in popularity for Los Muertos, threatening Portero under the name of King Viper. Soon after, Lumérico announced Portero was stepping down as their CEO, but internally, he had not officially resigned as many in the company still had faith in him. Meanwhile, Portero himself claimed he would be fully exonerated by the authorities in due time, which ended up being the case in spite of public outrage. Portero may have remained in power after Sombra's attack, but now all of México and the World at Large had no reason to trust him ever again, turning the Sombra Collective into a Robin Hood hero among the locals and even abroad, and fueling the ranks of Los Muertos even further.

Tracer's acts of charity around the Underworld quickly got the attention of none other than Tekhartha Mondatta, who had continued to advocate for Omnic rights around the world and especially in London, even after the Turing Green project fell apart. After sending a message to Tracer with Iggy, the two met and reconnected after all the years that had passed since the Uprising. Lena was unsure as to why she had been called, expressing unease at her unwelcome attempts to help the Omnic community, as she did not feel right was the right person to do it, yet also knew she couldn't just look away. Mondatta reassured her, explaining how those efforts were needed, as a way for humans and Omnics to move on and look forward, and invited Tracer to join him in the call for action.

As Mondatta prepared for his evening speech at Kings Row, Lena joined the massive crowd with Iggy and her gang. The group was ready to hear the Shamballi talk, but as he began his speech, Lena could not shake a bad feeling in her head, and as usual, her instincts were right. Tracer left the crowd and began to scout the Rooftops, where they found the Widowmaker, readying herself for the perfect shot at Mondatta. Tracer did her best to stop her, warning his bodyguards of the danger and prompting them to escort him out, but as she chased down the assassin, Widowmaker had lined a shot right through her chest. Instinctually, Tracer recalled dodging the bullet, only to find out she was never the target. Getting out of the way allowed the shot to kill Mondatta right as he was being escorted out, for all of his supporters to see.

Tracer confronted the assassin, enraged and confused as to why anyone would do this, but the Widowmaker merely cackled at the sheer euphoria of her killing, as she made her way to the Talon aircraft, leaving Lena behind with a Damaged Chronal Accelerator, barely avoiding Vigilante charges by the IJC, and having her relationship with Iggy soured as the Omnic blamed Tracer in her guilt and denial.

Over the years after Petra, Talon had an ongoing operation to track down and kill ex-Overwatch operatives, especially those who would still get in their way in spite of Petra's accords. Reyes spearheaded this hunt. In between his own personal agenda of murders, he would talk Overwatch targets by prioritizing those who had personally wronged him or got in his way during Overwatch. However, while there were many high profile agents that were easy to find, Talon intended to be more thorough, so they needed to access the official databases.

Winston was still settled in Gibraltar at the time, working on personal inventions and finding parts to help Lena with the Underworld grid. As usual, he kept watching global news and often found himself inches away from sending a recall message to all agents. As he was getting scolded by Athena, all of a sudden, Talon intruders made their way into his room. Winston killed the lights and took down many of the troops but struggled against the Reaper, who had installed a virus onto Athena's systems to download the Agent Database while his goons kept Winston Occupied.

When the data breach was nearly complete, Winston managed to catch Reaper by surprise with a failed barrier projector, causing a shock wave and leaving Reaper vulnerable enough to seemingly retreat, having only acquired a partial list of agents by the point. At the last minute, Winston was able to stop the breach, causing a restart that showed him the recall protocol from before. With Overwatch agents now directly in danger and having had enough years of waiting on the sidelines, Winston finally decided to start his recall, preparing a moving speech alongside it and sending it to all Operatives and Bases. While he did not expect many to answer immediately, the very first to reply was Lena herself, ready to bring on the cavalry to this new Overwatch.

Tracer answered the recall quickly but not in the best of circumstances. The protests that followed Mondatta's death quickly turned to riots, forcing the police to call in special Ops and resulting in the death of Lady, one of Iggy's friends, who got caught by a point-blank sonic pulse. The murder of their spiritual leader and now a victim of Police Brutality in their own community began to radicalize the Omnics of the Underworld, commanded by Kace, to start a revolution, and Tracer's Chronal Accelerator was malfunctioning from battle damage. Had it not been for Lizzy, another Omnic friend who stayed by her side and helped Emily fix up the device with Winston parts, Lena wouldn't have made it back home.

Things were not much better in the Underworld. While Iggy had pushed Lena aside and followed Kace's plans, she noticed things were escalating rather quickly, as he seemingly staged his own assassination attempt to equate himself to another Mondatta being silenced. He was plotting to lure the police into the Underworld and then blowing up the grid, and was willing to hold anyone who opposed him as a hostage. Iggy was able to warn Lizzy before getting captured herself for confronting Kace. She and Tracer made their way into the Underworld, where they were joined by Winston, and together they were able to free the hostages and rally the Omnics against Kace using the communication system to warn everyone of his plan to destroy the Underworld. 

As his supporters dropped their weapons, Kace pulled out a gun, and as a last resort, shot directly at the opposition, but Tracer blinked right in the way and took the bullet for Iggy. The repairs to her accelerator were only a temporary fix, and the damage caused her to recall in a loop, taking the bullet over and over. In the commotion, Kace managed to escape London, with no clue of who he worked for or where he went. Lena's efforts rallied the whole Omnic Community at the hospital while she recovered, and with Winston's help in repairing the grid, the duo managed to stop what could have very well gone down as a second Uprising.

Winston's recall was automatically sent not just to all Overwatch agents but also to their old bases, even those in disrepair. The signal reached Ecopoint: Antartica, although it was too weak to display in the damaged terminals. This message reactivated the remaining functional systems of the Ecopoint: and with it, Mei's cryogenic chamber opened. Nine years had passed since the base was lost to the super storm, yet Mei had not aged a day from the procedure. It took her a moment to realize she had been the only survivor in the whole base, now trapped in Antartica with nobody knowing she was alive.

Her only companion was the base's assistant drone, Snowball, and together they were able to get some of the systems running again, catching up to what had happened in the world and how Overwatch was disbanded. Mei knew that the power wouldn't last long, but if an emergency frequency by Overwatch had reached the Ecopoint, someone might be able to get them out, and with nine years worth of data of the uncontrolled anomaly prototype, it meant that if she got out, her team would not have died in vain.

With whatever parts she could find, Mei engineered a Cryogenic device that would help her climb up to the broken tower and catch the signal in her equipment, but the power gave how before it was completed. Seeing no other way out, Snowball hooked to the system and transferred its remaining battery to the base, buying Mei enough time to finish the device and climb up the tower. When the signal finally came into display, Mei was greeted by Winston's speech and able to answer the recall. After paying her respects to her deceased team, Mei left the Ecopoint: and ventured onto the continent, bringing Snowball along and hooking him to a solar panel. Together they traveled for days until they found a way out of Antartica and onto Gibraltar.

Four years had passed since Baptiste left Talon during the raid at Monte Cristi. Thinking he might finally be off the hook, he began to visit his hometown more, helping Ros with the patients at her clinic since they were experiencing a shortage due to Sinclair Pharmaceuticals raising prices. Later at night he frequented a local bar enough that one day, he was intercepted by two Talon agents, Trung Le Nguyen and none other than Mauga himself. While they presented themselves as friendly, Baptiste knew better than to trust them. Turns out they needed his help for a job. Vernard Sinclair, head of the same pharmaceutical company giving the clinic trouble, owed money to Talon, and while this alone wouldn't be enough to turn Baptiste around, Mauga revealed that he knew about Ros and her clinic. With her life possibly on the line, Baptiste had no choice but to collaborate.

The following morning, Baptiste met the two after going over the briefing, now wearing his old combat armor with the Talon insignia burnt off. They had a scheduled meeting, allowing them to walk inside until the private security surrounded them in the library, at which point hell broke loose. Once the trio stormed their way into Sinclair's office, the man had a bargain to offer for his life.

Sinclair was an ex Overwatch operative and days ago, he received a message from Winston himself. While in Overwatch, he would feed information to Talon, and was more than willing to give Intel on several agents if it saved his life. Nguyen had no interest in his deal however, as many ex-Overwatch operatives already worked in Talon, they could get that information elsewhere. Baptiste was disgusted by Sinclair, but if he ended his life there was no way back, he would have turned into the man he was running from all those years. So instead, he threw a flash bang and helped the man escape, in return asking him to give his products for free, unless he wanted Talon to know where he was. All the whole, Mauga chased Baptiste, still wanting to take him back to Talon, especially now that he had compromised the mission. Baptiste feigned surrender, before detonating a device that destroyed the pier, using his immortality field to dampen the blow on himself, and allowing him to escape on a boat in the commotion. He may have escaped Talon this time, but now he knew Overwatch agents were in danger. He had to warm those he knew, starting with Dr. Ziegler. And in order to do so, he needed some contact, even if it meant reaching out to Sombra.

While Overwatch bases were decommissioned, not all of them were taken apart completely, and even of those that remain, not all of them were given to Helix. Ecopoint: Monterrey had been constructed under the ocean with the intention of monitoring marine life. It was built to withstand deep Sea pressure for years without needing major maintenance, and its infrastructure was solid enough to hold even after it was abandoned.

In such a specific case, the Ecopoint: was never fully decommissioned, and it ended up becoming an attraction site for submersible Omnics, urban explorers and general thrill seekers daring enough to dive to the facilities, entering through an insecure port in the hydroponic section.

As people explored a completely unguarded Overwatch base, many began to report strange movement in the water off the view ports. Something else lived there, it twisted and bent off the corners of the cameras, and it consistently fled from the light. While there's no solid proof that these divers weren't just making things up or getting scared by shadows in a haunted house, it caught a lot of attention from conspiracy theories and cryptid hunters, prompting local authorities to increase harbor patrols on the water above, both to prevent people from diving again, and to keep a close eye on whatever was lurking in those waters.

Kiriko's family wasn't the only ones brave enough to defy the Hashimoto rule in Kanezaka, as many of the young residents who grew up after the Shimada era were not as willing to bend down to any clan like their ancestors. Ryota, Sakura and Nobuto all had their own personal grievances with what the Hashimoto had done to their community and even their own families, and because of it they often ended up confronting the thugs against the odds.

One night, the group confronted a Hashimoto enforcer pestering the owner of their local Ramen shop, when suddenly the lights were cut out and a ninja figure attacked from the shadows, incapacitating the Hashimoto. The masked hero was none other than Kiriko, who was keeping an eye on the teens for a while, protecting them with the Fox Anima. As she continued her patrol later that night, she spotted the same group being abducted into a car by the Hashimoto, who still had unfinished business with the kids.

Kiriko tracked the vehicle into the Hashimoto base where she found them at the mercy of Keigo Kuroura, the head of the Kanezaka branch. Kiriko battled Kuroura himself, quickly overwhelming him as his poor-quality anima blade was no match for Toshiro's masterpiece, the Fox. Once defeated, he attempted to call the headquarters for reinforcements, but Ryota had already crashed his phone, allowing the kids to escape. Kiriko's actions not only saved the teenagers, but inspired them to continue fighting now that they had seen someone else, not that much older, going toe to toe against one of the Clan higher ups. Ryota took a job as a busboy at the ramen shop, using his position as a way to gather Intel, and encouraging his friends to train so they could all help the protector of Kanezaka one day.

Mei eventually found her way to Gibraltar and reunited with Winston and Tracer, but given she wasn't a trained fighter, she couldn't do much to help them on the field. What she could do, however, was reestablish the ecological network systems from the old era. Overwatch had several bases and outposts around the world with the express purpose of environmental monitoring and if they truly wanted to get back, they would need more than just fighters, but also scientists, and it just so happens, Mei had nine years word of meteorological data that could help with restoring entire ecosystems and studying other anomalies.

Winston suggested starting writing a journal of her travels, posting it online for people to see her unique perspective, as someone who was coming back from being frozen in time. After improving her portable cryogenic technology, she set off on adventure, writing everything down and slowly becoming more confident throughout her journey. From the heights of Mount Logan to the depths of Asia and even up to the frozen peaks of the Himalayas, Mei began testing her equipment around the world, studying local wildlife, even reaching a neat of an endangered species up in the Attic and appearing on the news giving her forecasts for upcoming super storms. It also wasn't all just work, as from time to time she would take detours into the nearby cities like Hollywood, catching up with years' worth of history and culture.

Mei's Travel log not only helped her mentally, get readjusted to the modern world and keep her occupied after the loss of her team, it also brought attention to many ecological issues still plaguing the world years after Overwatch fell. For many readers who couldn't leave their home, it served as a way to learn about the world, while for others, it was a reminder of a better time, where Overwatch actively worked towards healing the planet, not just fighting criminals.

During Zenyatta's Pilgrimage to Suravasa, he continued to meditate on the last conversation he had with his master, Mondatta, and his closer friend, Rammattra, as their words still wondered in his mind all these years later. Suddenly, he found himself surrounded by Talon agents, led by Widowmaker and Sombra, who were sent to arrange a meeting with the Monk and Null Sector's leader. The ongoing invasion had lasted months and ravaged Omnic communities across the world, so Zenyatta was quite conflicted about what his older brother would have to say, but without much of a choice, Zenyatta agreed, and was escorted into King's Row, the place of their master's death, by the very same woman who pulled the trigger.

Ramattra dismissed the two agents, wishing to talk in private with his brother. Ramattra reminisced of their old master, his teachings and advocacy for coexistence, a naïve belief. As he explained his reasons to Zenyatta, he told him how he followed in Aurora's footsteps in trying to answer the question: How to save a world that refuses to be saved? Zenyatta immediately argued that Null Sector also spread suffering and hatred, yet Ramattra insisted his actions are but a fraction of human cruelty. In a final attempt to convince his brother, he tells him the invasion was a means to attach Mind Uploading devices to Omnic Skulls, in order to save and preserve them. Had it not been for Overwatch, he could have saved many thousands more, but he had still managed to retrieve a large enough amount to begin the next steps of his plan, so all that was left was retreating to his base, while Talon took care of the rest.

Ramattra asked one final time for his brother to join him in this next phase, alongside the rest of their kin, but Zenyatta still rejected him, unable to look past Ramattra's alliance with Talon, the people responsible for Mondatta's death, even if Ramattra continued to claim he held no sympathy for their greed for conflict. Still, Zenyatta had chosen his own path, believing that peace with humanity was possible. He urged Ramattra to not give up on them completely, and that Mondatta's preaching was not in vain. Ramattra, expectedly disagreed, taking pity on humanity and their misbegotten civilization. So, as they wished the best for each other, and their dreams of peace, they simply parted ways.
